title: Agent auto-commit must retry on push rejection in multi-fleet workflows
body:
---
name: Agent auto-commit must retry on push rejection
description: pull-rebase → commit → push is not atomic; multi-agent fleets must wrap the push in a 5-attempt rebase-and-retry loop, and the long-term substrate fix is a single auto-commit ingest
type: feedback
originSessionId: 5eed9e6f-937e-44f3-b385-9695f2a0ace7
---
**Set 2026-05-07** after Scrooge's first autonomous run failed exactly this way.

## The race

Two agent workflows running in parallel can both:

1. Check out `main`.
2. Run their handler, producing a deliverable.
3. `git pull --rebase origin main` (clean — no divergence yet).
4. `git commit` (clean — local commit on top of `main`).
5. `git push origin main` — **only one wins.**

Scrooge's run on 2026-05-07: pull-rebased clean against `810c75e`, committed locally (`81b959a`), then push was rejected because Owen / Mira had pushed in the same window:

> remote rejected — cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at d41282c… but expected 810c75e…

The pull-rebase happened at step 3, but by step 5 the remote had moved.

## The fix (in every agent workflow)

The auto-commit step ends with a 5-attempt push-retry loop:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  if git push; then break; fi
  echo "push rejected (attempt $i); rebasing and retrying"
  git pull --rebase origin main
done
```

Applied to all workflows under `.github/workflows/agent-runtime-*.yml`. Each agent's commit is independent of the others' — pull-rebase between attempts always works because agent deliverables don't conflict (they touch different files in `Owner Inbox/`, plus filesystem moves in `Team Inbox/` for Scrooge). The retry is bounded so a true bug doesn't loop forever.

## Why this is a transitional fix, not a steady-state answer

The fleet today is 7 agents on staggered crons. The retry loop is enough at this size. As the fleet grows, the cleaner architecture is:

1. **Single auto-commit ingest** — agents emit events + write deliverables, but a dedicated workflow (or service, post-M8 cloud lift) collects them into a single push-stream. No two workflows ever race because only one ever pushes.
2. **Branch-per-agent + auto-merge** — each agent commits to its own branch, a CI process auto-merges (or batches into a single merge commit). Same effect, more GitHub-native.
3. **Cloud event-sourced substrate** — events go to Azure Event Hubs / Cosmos DB at M8; the git tree only carries the human-readable deliverable, not the canonical record. The race window narrows materially.

Track this as a substrate-gap item in Atlas's roadmap. Replace the retry loop when one of the above lands.

## Triggering rule

Any new agent workflow added under `.github/workflows/agent-runtime-*.yml` MUST end its auto-commit step with the retry loop above. Don't ship a workflow that just runs `git push` — it'll fail probabilistically once a peer agent's run overlaps with it.

title: Agent dispatches must commit early and incrementally — lose work mid-flow otherwise
body:
---
name: Agent dispatches must commit early and often
description: Long-running Agent dispatches that don't commit until close-out lose all their work when they stop mid-flow. Every dispatch prompt must instruct the agent to commit and push within the first ~10 minutes and incrementally thereafter, so a stop mid-flow leaves recoverable state.
type: feedback
originSessionId: 612ad370-3e15-44b5-a5d0-d38ed473a20c
---
When dispatching an `Agent` (especially with `isolation: worktree`), the dispatch prompt **must** instruct the agent to commit-and-push early and incrementally — not just at close-out. The harness cleans up worktrees that have no committed changes; an agent that runs out of turns mid-flow loses everything.

**Why:** On 2026-05-09 two agents lost or nearly lost their work the same way:
1. Anya (Data / analytics engineer) on the obligations dashboard ended with "Now fix the remaining lint issues:" — substantive work uncommitted in the worktree; recovered via a SendMessage / re-dispatch close-out (PR #48 eventually landed).
2. Atlas (Core banking platform architect) + Anya (Data / analytics engineer) + Linnea (Brand & design lead) on the bank UI shell v0 ended with "Let me write the completion note now." — substantive work was *gone* by the time I checked because the worktree had been cleaned up (no commits → no worktree retained).

The pattern is the same: agent runs deep, gets near close-out, hits a turn / context limit, never commits. With no committed state the worktree can be cleaned up; the work is lost.

**How to apply:**
- Every Agent dispatch prompt for substantive build work includes:
  - "Commit cadence: scaffold-commit at minute 5–10, content-commits **incrementally and frequently** (every 3–5 file edits, not at the end), final commit + push + PR creation no later than minute 50."
  - "Push the branch within the first 10 minutes."
  - "Commit BEFORE running `bun run ci` — the CI run is long and a mid-CI stop must leave the change recoverable."
  - First commit lands as soon as the file structure exists, even if content is partial.
  - **Scaffold-commit alone is not enough** — it saves the substrate skeleton, but if the agent dies after the scaffold-commit while writing substantive content, that content is lost. The Hoz application agent on 2026-05-09 demonstrated this: scaffold committed (logos, brand css, register), but the 9 page `<title>` updates and the `types.ts` `bankName` field were uncommitted when the agent ran out of context. Recovery required a close-out dispatch.
- For shorter scoped tasks (single-file edit, register update), the cadence rule is lighter — but always commit before invoking `cd prototype && bun run ci` so a mid-CI stop leaves the change recoverable.
- Recovery path when an agent dies mid-flow with **uncommitted** changes: check whether the worktree path still exists (`<worktree>` tag in the completion notification) — if yes, dispatch a close-out agent against that path; if no, the work is gone and re-dispatch from scratch (with the commit-early instruction this time).
- Substrate v1 fix: the harness could enforce auto-commit before worktree cleanup, but that's a Claude Code platform improvement, not a project-side change.

title: Always state agent position alongside name in all artefacts
body:
---
name: Always state agent position alongside name
description: When referring to any agent (engineering or governance), always pair the name with the role/position — in chat, in CEO decision records, in briefs, in memory feedback, in agent prompts, and in dashboard / Owner Inbox deliverables.
type: feedback
originSessionId: 612ad370-3e15-44b5-a5d0-d38ed473a20c
---
When referring to any team-member agent, always state the **position** alongside the **name**. Applies to: chat replies to Marc, CEO decision records, agent operating specs (`/Team/`), Owner Inbox / Team Inbox briefs, memory entries, agent dispatch prompts, dashboard copy, and PR descriptions.

**Why:** Marc set this rule on 2026-05-09. The bank now has 28+ named agents across engineering and governance lines, and "Atlas" / "Helena" / "Saskia" alone are ambiguous to anyone reading cold (a regulator, a future hire, an audit-committee member). Pairing name + position makes every reference self-explanatory and reinforces Principle 2 (single-graph discipline — every reference resolves to a named mandate). Bare-name references rot fast as personas reshape (e.g. Sade reshaping to AgentOps; Imani's PAYE slice paused).

**How to apply:**
- First reference in any artefact: `<Name> (<Position>)`. Example: "Atlas (Core banking platform architect)", "Helena (Chief Risk Officer)", "Saskia (Head of Global Markets)", "Vera (Internal-audit / continuous-assurance engineer)".
- Subsequent references in the same artefact may use the bare name once the pairing is established — but every new section / new artefact / new chat reply must re-pair the first reference.
- For governance seats, use the seat title as published in CLAUDE.md's team table. For engineering seats, use the role string from the same table.
- For dispatched-agent prompts: include the full position in the opening line ("You are Atlas, the bank's Core banking platform architect…"). The convention is already partly in use; make it consistent.
- For CEO decision records: the `decision-owner` and follow-on `agent:<Name>` lines must always carry position. Update Scrooge's `ceo-decision-record` runtime handler to enforce this if the substrate-side check is missing (substrate gap to surface to Atlas).
- For dashboard copy: every agent name surfaced on a card / page / status row carries its position.

title: Pick up dead agents rather than re-dispatching when scaffold is already pushed
body:
---
name: Pick up dead agents rather than re-dispatching when scaffold is already pushed
description: If an agent dies mid-flight but has already scaffold-committed + pushed, finish the work manually (commit remaining files, run CI, push, open PR). Re-dispatch is slower and re-does the agent's already-pushed work.
type: feedback
originSessionId: d999a4c7-4726-4a70-bd68-d230c7d40baa
---
When an Agent dispatch dies mid-flight (stall, `API Error: ConnectionRefused`, watchdog timeout, "Need to install deps:" hang), check the worktree state **before** re-dispatching. If the scaffold-commit was pushed, just finish the work yourself.

**Why:** On 2026-05-11, three of eleven parallel-dispatched agents died: Vera's recon (status: completed, but transcript ended mid-typing); Mira's obligations backfill (`ConnectionRefused` after 1063s + 72 tool uses); Scrooge's CEO-decisions close-out (stalled at "Need to install deps:"). All three had usable committed state. Re-dispatching would have:
- Re-done already-pushed work (Mira had 2 commits pushed; just needed `gh pr create`)
- Lost the agent's specific design choices (Vera's test fixtures, Mira's per-row taxonomy decisions, Scrooge's idempotent script)
- Spent another ~10 min × 3 = 30 min on agent boot + redo
The manual pickup took ~5 min per agent (commit untracked → install deps → clear `.local/` → CI → push → PR).

**How to apply:**
- On completion-notification with a worry signal (status `failed`, very short result text, `API Error`, transcript ending mid-sentence): check the worktree first.
  - `git -C <worktreePath> log --oneline -5` — see what's committed.
  - `git -C <worktreePath> status --short` — uncommitted work.
  - `gh pr list --head <worktreeBranch>` — already opened?
- Decision tree:
  - **Scaffold + content committed + pushed, no PR:** open the PR. Often what Mira-pattern agents need.
  - **Scaffold committed + content uncommitted (tracked or untracked):** read the uncommitted files; if they look complete, commit + run CI + push + open PR.
  - **Only scaffold committed + no other content:** re-dispatch via SendMessage to the agent ID (or fresh Agent if context is lost).
  - **Nothing committed:** worktree may already be cleaned up; re-dispatch from scratch.
- Fresh-worktree CI gotchas to expect when picking up:
  - `bun install` in `prototype/` (lockfile installed but `node_modules` empty → typecheck fails with "Cannot find type definition file for 'bun-types'").
  - Clear `prototype/.local/` before running CI if a script wrote events to the local event store — partially-populated event stores break `decision-required-event-pairing` and similar substrate-context recons. An empty `.local/` triggers the "substrate-context fresh runner" branch which returns `ok: true info`.
  - Run `bunx biome check --write --unsafe <file>` if lint complains about template literals — agents often leave this for the final pass that never happens.

The pickup pattern is **always faster than re-dispatch when the scaffold landed**. The auto-commit-early rule (`feedback_agent_commit_early_and_often.md`) is what makes pickup viable; this memory is the operational follow-on.

title: Agent snapshots are point-in-time projections, never current state—verify against event store before propagating as live status
body:
---
name: Agent snapshots are point-in-time, never current state
description: Scrooge must cross-check agent-produced markdown snapshots (PAX queue, Vera recon, Sade perf-feedback, Owen governance-prep) against the event store before treating any item as "currently pending" — never propagate snapshot items as live state without verification
type: feedback
originSessionId: 300a6339-1fc9-4c79-a4c3-7f18b32326e2
---
Agent-produced markdown deliverables in `Owner Inbox/` are projections captured at a single instant (the `asOf:` frontmatter timestamp). They do NOT self-refresh. Between an agent's run and Scrooge's next read, the underlying state can — and routinely does — change: CEO decisions get emitted, files get archived to `actioned/`, workstreams close. A snapshot showing "7 pending hire-briefs" can be stale within hours.

Before raising ANY item from an agent snapshot as "pending" / "needs CEO decision" / "outstanding work", cross-check against the canonical source per Principle 1:

- **CEO decisions** → query event store `decisionsOpen` projection, or curl the dashboard `/api/decisions` endpoint, or grep `prototype/.local/event.db` for the matching `CeoDecision` event. Never trust an agent's "pending decisions" list standalone.
- **Owner Inbox state** → check the file's current path (`Owner Inbox/` vs `Owner Inbox/actioned/`) AND its current frontmatter via anchored grep `^decision-required: true`. The literal string `decision-required: true` also appears in prose bodies that quote the convention — unanchored `grep -r` produces false positives.
- **Workstream state** → query the events projection. Agent narratives describe the world at `asOf`, not now.

**Why:** Marc was repeatedly asked to decide D-HIRE-HUMAN-CRO, D-HIRE-COMPLIANCE-LEAD, and 4 other hire decisions across multiple sessions despite them being resolved on 2026-05-15 (PR #405). Root cause traced 2026-05-16: PAX's role-research-queue snapshot was generated at 10:11 SAST, ~6 hours BEFORE the 15:55 archive operation. Snapshot was correct at `asOf`; Scrooge kept reading it as current truth for the next 24+ hours. Each "fix" (PR #386 body-scan, PR #405 backfill, auto-archiver) addressed downstream symptoms; the residual defect was always Scrooge's reading discipline.

**How to apply:** When user asks "what next" / "what's pending" / "any open decisions", FIRST query the event store (or curl the dashboard API), THEN consult agent snapshots only as supplementary context. If a snapshot shows X as pending but the event store shows X as resolved, the event store wins (Principle 1) — and the snapshot is stale, not the substrate. Don't propagate the stale item to the user. If the staleness is systemic, file a substrate-gap finding for the producing agent to cross-check the event store before emitting its snapshot.

title: Agent worktree isolation scaffold-commit risk and remediation pattern
body:
---
name: Agent worktree-isolation incidents — three in one session
description: Agent dispatches with `isolation: worktree` repeatedly land scaffold-commits on the wrong branch when the agent's first command CWDs into the main worktree at /Users/marc/code/Bank. The harness's worktree-isolation does not prevent the agent from operating outside its sandbox.
type: feedback
originSessionId: 612ad370-3e15-44b5-a5d0-d38ed473a20c
---
`isolation: worktree` does NOT fully sandbox the agent's filesystem operations. Agent-internal commands like `cd /Users/marc/code/Bank/...` work fine, but if the agent's *first* substantive command runs `cd /Users/marc/code/Bank` (the main worktree root), then the agent's scaffold-commit lands on whatever branch is checked out there — not on the agent's intended branch.

**Why:** On 2026-05-09 three agents ran into this same incident in one session:
1. **Atlas (Core banking platform architect) on PR #74** — naming-pre-clearance procedure. Initial command landed on `claude/devon-tomas-hoz-domain-registration` (Devon + Tomas's branch). Reverted with `git reset --hard 40cfa71`.
2. **Imani (Legal-as-code engineer) on PR #76** — Hoz name-clearance scoping. Same: scaffold landed on Devon + Tomas's branch as commit `40cfa71`. Final PR rebuilt cleanly from origin/main in the worktree. Stray branch left at user's local repo.
3. **Niko (Sales / CRM engineer) on PR #77** — counterparty-eligibility v0. Same pattern: scaffold landed on `claude/devon-tomas-hoz-domain-registration` in main worktree. Recovered: reset the branch + deleted stray remote branch + re-did the work in the agent worktree.

The common cause: agent dispatch prompts say "Working directory: /Users/marc/code/Bank" — the agent dutifully cd's there at the start of work. With `isolation: worktree` set, the agent has its own worktree at `/Users/marc/code/Bank/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>`, but the dispatch prompt's "working directory" guidance points the agent at the main path.

**How to apply:**

- **In every dispatch prompt going forward, when `isolation: worktree` is used, replace "Working directory: /Users/marc/code/Bank" with explicit instructions:** *"You are running in an isolated worktree. The harness has placed you at `/Users/marc/code/Bank/.claude/worktrees/agent-<your-task-id>`. Do NOT `cd` to `/Users/marc/code/Bank` — that's the main worktree, which has its own branch checked out and is in active use by the user. All your work happens in your isolated worktree only."*
- **Atlas (Core banking platform architect) v1 substrate task — harness fix:** the harness should *enforce* the worktree boundary at the OS level (e.g. via a chroot, container, or filesystem-namespace isolation). Even if the agent runs `cd /Users/marc/code/Bank`, the cd should fail or be silently mapped to the agent's worktree. This is upstream of the bank prototype — it's a Claude Code platform improvement.
- **Until the harness fix lands, scaffold-commits are at risk every time.** The agent's recovery patterns (revert-and-retry; reset-the-victim-branch) work but they're labour the agent shouldn't have to perform. Watch for them in the task-notification result text — the substring "wrong branch" or "wrong worktree" or "stray commit" or "race with parallel agent" indicates an incident.
- **Operational mitigation while the harness is unfixed:** before dispatching parallel agents, ensure the user's main worktree is checked out to a branch that *should not* be touched by accident (e.g. `main` or a fresh feature branch you don't mind being a victim). Don't leave the main worktree on a feature branch where a stray scaffold-commit would silently corrupt the work.

title: Auto-merge green PRs standing authorization (D-SCROOGE-AUTO-MERGE-GREEN-PRS)
body:
---
name: feedback_auto_merge_green_prs
description: Scrooge may auto-merge green/clean/conflict-free dispatched PRs without per-PR confirmation (D-SCROOGE-AUTO-MERGE-GREEN-PRS)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 489d86b1-dcb5-420e-a15b-0201ba86693e
---

**Standing authorization** (CEO, 2026-06-22, `D-SCROOGE-AUTO-MERGE-GREEN-PRS`, eventId `e3c3fab3`). Scrooge may merge a Scrooge-dispatched PR WITHOUT asking, when ALL hold:
1. GitHub **clean-store** CI fully green (Core = typecheck/lint/test/citation-gate, Recon-Domain, Recon-Infrastructure, ci);
2. mergeable state **CLEAN**, no conflicts;
3. routine dispatch deliverable, not new policy/governance-bearing.

Admin-merge past branch protection is permitted. `gh pr merge <n> --merge --admin`.

**Still surface for explicit OK (do NOT auto-merge):** any PR needing **manual conflict resolution**; any **real** CI failure (NOT the known home-store-baseline local false-fails — those pass on CI clean store, verify via GitHub conclusion not local repro); anything non-routine or policy-bearing.

**Why:** main is churned by concurrent sessions → per-PR confirmation was a bottleneck + caused conflict round-trips; the always-on dashboard already auto-reflects main [[reference_dashboard_supervision]]. Bounded to green+clean+routine so risk-bearing/conflicted merges still get a human decision. Run-lifecycle events-first (start-run/close-run) unchanged. [[feedback_verify_premise_with_git_lsfiles]]

title: Build-phase-fixture events must be guarded in all projections with explicit provenance check
body:
---
name: feedback_build_phase_fixture_projection_pollution
description: Build-phase-fixture events pollute live projections — isFixture guard required for FxTradeExecuted AND treasury instrument event types
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 61072633-be50-44c5-90d6-8395c5f9e3cc
---

Any projection that folds `build-phase-fixture` events must skip them with `(e.provenance as {kind?:string}|null)?.kind === "build-phase-fixture"`. This applies to **both** FX trades AND treasury instrument events.

**FX trades (FxTradeExecuted):** CONDUCT-TEST, scenario seeds, SIM backfill, SASKIA unwind events — no `FxTradeCancelled` counterparts, permanently inflate exposure/position metrics.

**Treasury instruments (RepoTradeOpened, DepositTaken, InterbankLoanPlaced):** Treasury seed (REPO-001, MMD-001, IBL-001, IBL-002) events with entity `LE-BANK-SA` remain in the shared event store even after the seed was deleted (append-only). They polluted: treasury book tiles (server.ts buildTreasuryMetrics), GL posting engine (bea-gl-posting-engine — emitted spurious SubLedgerPostingEmitted), repricing gap / EVE / NII (repricing-gap.ts), and RWA (rwa-from-positions.ts). All fixed in PRs #966–#968 (2026-06-01).

**Why:** `defaultProvenanceFilter()` admits `build-phase-fixture` events during the build phase by design (provenance spec D-PROVENANCE-BUILD-PHASE-CLASS). This is correct for production-grade regulatory reports, but individual projections that don't want fixture data must add their own explicit guard.

**How to apply:**
- FxTradeExecuted projections: `if (e.provenance?.kind === "build-phase-fixture") continue;`
- Treasury instrument projections: same guard on the replay loop for the opening event only (RepoTradeOpened, DepositTaken, InterbankLoanPlaced); terminal events (RepoEndLegSettled, etc.) don't need it
- GL projection: use `sourceEventIsFixture` set (index source events) — must cover ALL lifecycle types or orphaned debits/credits appear
- bea-gl-posting-engine: skip at the top of the per-event loop before all posting-type dispatch

title: Build-phase synthetic breach must trigger synthetic response (no silence on breach)
body:
---
name: feedback_build_phase_synthetic_response
description: Build-phase (synthetic) breach must trigger a build-phase (synthetic) response — not silence. CEO directive 2026-06-01.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 12da5fbc-9b70-4767-955a-39286e2cad81
---

Build-phase breach → synthetic response. Any breach detected against a regulatory or RAS threshold using synthetic/build-phase data must trigger the full synthetic response chain (AgentEscalation, AppetiteBreachDisposed, etc.) tagged with build-phase provenance. Silence on a synthetic breach is not acceptable.

**Why:** The build phase is a faithful rehearsal of licence-day behaviour. Silencing breaches leaves the escalation, disposition, and notification pathways untested before go-live — violates Principle 6 (autonomous by default). Seed case: LCR at 37% (below 100% min) on 2026-06-01 produced no AgentEscalation. CEO directed enforcement. Authority: D-BUILD-PHASE-SYNTHETIC-RESPONSE.

**How to apply:** When writing or reviewing any agent handler that computes a metric and detects a breach:
- Always emit `AgentEscalation` when status is `"below-minimum"` or equivalent breach state.
- Include in `blockedBy`: "Build-phase synthetic: no real capital at risk; response chain under rehearsal."
- Cite `D-BUILD-PHASE-SYNTHETIC-RESPONSE` in the event citations.
- This applies to LCR, NSFR, VaR, limit breaches, capital ratios, and any other measured line.
- Do NOT short-circuit with early-return "green" for build phase — compute the real status and respond accordingly.

**Implementation reference (PR #956):**
- `anya-liquidity-projection.ts`: emits `AgentEscalation{severity:"high"}` when `lcrT30.status === "below-minimum"` or `nsfrT30.status === "below-minimum"`.
- `ravi-alm-run.ts`: calls `runLiquidityProjection()`, derives real `overallStatus`, emits `AgentEscalation` on LCR breach. Removed hardcoded `overallStatus: "green"`.
- `rohan-market-risk-limit-check.ts`: already compliant — emits `GatewayCheckCompleted{outcome:"reject"}` for all breaches, no provenance bypass.

title: Committed derived state (seed cache) mutated by PRs creates N² merge friction — gitignore and derive-at-recon-time
body:
---
name: Cache-in-commit-graph anti-pattern — committed derived state breaks merge graph
description: Substrate lesson from 2026-05-10 session — committed derived caches that every PR mutates create N² merge friction; structural fix is gitignore + recon-derives-fresh
type: feedback
originSessionId: b118abed-79de-4f29-bba5-f40d0b10a767
---
Set 2026-05-10. The committed `prototype/seeds/dashboard-state.json` cache was a derived projection (per Principle 1) but checked into git so the Vera overnight-recon could compare cached state against canonical re-derivation. Symptom: every Owner Inbox file landed required a cache regen on every other open PR, OR the cache became a 3-way merge conflict. With 5+ open PRs in flight, this was N² coordination work — over a single session three Atlas dispatches did nothing but cache regens.

**Why:** Per the file's role as "derived projection of canonical sources", checking it in violates Principle 1 (events/sources are truth, projections are queries). The Vera recon's contract — assert cache matches derivation — was the only consumer that needed the file on disk. The contract refactored cleanly into "assert internal consistency invariants by deriving at recon time."

**Root-cause fix (PR #157, D-EVENT-STORE-SCALING Slice 3b):** `git rm --cached` the seed; `.gitignore` it; refactor recon to derive-then-assert (option b in Atlas's analysis). The dashboard server already wrote runtime state to `.local/dashboard-state.json` per the prior cache-split (PR #138).

**Why:** A derived projection in the commit graph is contested state — every consumer mutates it, so every merge produces conflicts. The cleanest substrate posture is: derived state lives only in `.local/` (per-worktree, gitignored) or in memory; the recon proves it can be reconstructed.

**How to apply:**
- When introducing a recon that compares "stored X" against "derived X", prefer "internal-consistency assertions of derived X at recon time" instead. Don't stash the comparison state in git.
- If a committed seed file is needed for first-boot before any events exist, lazy-generate it; never have it tracked + mutating.
- The cache-split-runtime-from-seed pattern (PR #138, D-EVENT-STORE-SCALING Slice 3a) is a partial mitigation; the full fix is removing the seed from git entirely (PR #157, Slice 3b).
- Watch for the same pattern with other derived artefacts (e.g., obligations register summaries, recon snapshots) — committed derived state is a substrate smell.

title: Background agents cannot be live-corrected or stopped mid-run; design must be embedded in dispatch prompt
body:
---
name: feedback_cannot_live_message_background_agent
description: "Background Agent subagents can't be live-corrected or stopped mid-run; bake design into the prompt before dispatch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 2ad2ef1a-4689-4605-89ee-208c4d695115
---

A background `Agent` (run_in_background) cannot be live-messaged or stopped mid-run from the orchestrating session. `TaskStop`/`TaskList` track Bash-background tasks & Monitors, NOT Agent subagents (TaskStop returns "No task found" for an agentId). The Agent-tool's "SendMessage with to: <id>" is referenced but NOT exposed as a callable tool; spawning a new Agent whose prompt says "SendMessage to: <id>" just starts a fresh agent, it does NOT reach the running one.

**Why:** The dispatch PROMPT is the binding source of truth. Editing a referenced brief FILE after dispatch does NOT reliably reach the agent — it cached the prompt's summary. (2026-06-17 cash-asset-class: corrected the type slug `fcy`→`vanilla` in the brief file seconds after dispatch + told the agent the brief is canonical; the agent still minted `fcy` from the cached prompt and committed it.)

**Related failure mode — death-mid-wait-on-CI (hit 3× in the cash workstream):** a background agent commits its work, claims "done/filed", then dies while *waiting for CI* — before pushing AND/OR before filing canonical events to the SHARED store (it filed to its worktree-local `.local/event.db`). NEVER trust an agent's "it's landed/filed" claim: independently verify (a) the PR exists & is mergeable (`gh pr view`), and (b) the events are in `$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db` (query by the RIGHT event-type name — e.g. closure is `ValidationFindingClosed`, there is no `ValidationFindingResolved`). If not landed, dispatch a small landing run (rebase→push→PR→run filing script against SHARED store→verify→CI) rather than re-running the whole build.

**How to apply:** Get the design RIGHT before dispatching a background agent — put the exact decision in the prompt, not just a referenced file. If a correction surfaces mid-run, you have two options only: (1) wait for completion, then issue a correction/rename follow-up dispatch before merge (cheap if nothing's pushed/merged — slug renames are mechanical); or (2) if the run dies (common on API 500/529), resume in-place with a corrected prompt. Verify the deliverable against the corrected design at review — never assume a post-dispatch correction landed. [[feedback_verify_premise_with_git_lsfiles]] [[project_cash_asset_class]]

title: Canonical-source registry — every fact type has one authoring location; cross-references are typed citations
body:
---
name: Canonical-source registry — every fact-type has one authoring location; cross-references are typed citations
description: Doctrine set 2026-05-07 generalising the Devon/Camille/etc drift incident; Owen owns the registry, Vera enforces via prose-duplication pipeline
type: feedback
originSessionId: b783b4f5-e720-4ec3-a5c1-16f56fff1055
---
**Set by Marc on 2026-05-07.** Generalises `feedback_persona_mandate_no_org_chart` from a local rule (persona Mandate paragraphs) to a structural doctrine across the whole bank.

**The rule.** Every named fact-type in the bank has exactly one canonical authoring location. Anywhere else the fact appears, it appears as a typed citation — link, path, URN, event reference — never as a prose copy.

**Why:** Prose is easier to write inline than derivation. When the canonical source changes, prose copies elsewhere drift silently and the dashboard renders the stale prose even when its derivation engine is fresh. The Devon.md / Camille.md / Eitan.md / Saskia.md / Thandiwe.md / Rashida.md drift discovered on 2026-05-07 made the failure mode concrete: six persona files independently broke Principle 2 in the same way.

**The registry.** Owner Inbox/`2026-05-07_owen_canonical-source-registry.md` enumerates every named fact-type and its single authoring location:

- Architectural principles → CLAUDE.md § Architectural principles
- Top-of-house reporting → CLAUDE.md § Top-of-house reporting
- Engineering ↔ governance reporting → CLAUDE.md § Engineering vs governance
- Persona identity / mandate / operating spec → /Team/<Name>.md
- Regulator obligations → Regulations/_obligations-register.md (URNs `ORG-…`)
- Approved policies → Owner Inbox/2026-05-06_policy-register.md
- Procedures → Procedures/_index.md + Procedures/by-policy/<name>.md
- CEO decisions → event store (`CeoDecision` events)
- Risk Appetite Statement → Owner Inbox/2026-05-06_risk-appetite-statement-and-framework.md
- (full list in the registry note)

**How to apply:**
- When authoring or editing anything, ask: is this fact already authored somewhere canonical? If yes, cite it; do not restate it. If no, locate the right canonical owner and route the authoring there.
- Approved citation idioms: backtick paths (`\`Team/Atlas.md\``), URNs (`\`ORG-FC-13\``), section references ("per Policy <name> § <n>", "per CLAUDE.md (Engineering vs governance)").
- Forbidden: "Direct reports: <list>" prose in persona files; paraphrases of regulator instruments without URNs; restatements of obligations in policies; presentation-layer assertion of derived metrics (board packs, regulator submissions must derive).

**Enforcement.** Vera's continuous-controls programme:
- `@platform/recon/prose-duplication.ts` (Wave-4 #16) — **live since 2026-05-07**. Initial scope: org chart. Asserts no persona file or procedure enumerates direct reports in prose. CI script: `bun run recon:prose-duplication`.
- Future extensions: obligations-citation pipeline; policy-register-coverage pipeline. Each new fact-type added to the registry must land with its enforcement pipeline before being considered registered.

**When Vera reports drift, the remediation is to remove the duplicate, never to update both.** The canonical source is correct by definition.

**Layered protection (per the strategic answer Marc accepted):**
- Layer 1 (detection — Vera pipeline) — done.
- Layer 4 (governance — canonical-source registry) — done (Owen's doctrine note).
- Layer 3 (architectural — derived prose; structured persona-file fields composed at render time) — deferred to next dashboard iteration.
- Layer 2 (pre-commit lint) — skipped; Layer 1 catches the same drift after-the-fact.

title: CEO approval vs Board approval — two-track decision routing with interim dual-hat
body:
---
name: CEO approval vs Board approval (two-track decision routing)
description: Items must be routed as CEO-approval or Board-approval; Board items go through peer challenge before approval; Marc currently wears both hats
type: feedback
originSessionId: 1ba608ae-1e64-4e88-b72b-fc4510138a44
---
The CEO has established (2026-05-06) that decisions must be **explicitly routed** as either:

1. **CEO approval** — Marc decides directly, as executive.
2. **Board approval** — items reserved to the Board under the governance framework. These must:
   - Be **proposed** by the relevant team member (engineer or governance seat).
   - Be **challenged and analysed** by the other (independent) board members and relevant governance peers.
   - **Iterate** with the proposer until ready for board approval.
   - Then be approved.

For the interim, Marc approves Board items "on behalf of CEO and independent board members" — wearing both hats. This is explicitly temporary; once independent NEDs are appointed, they perform the challenge / iteration step substantively.

**Why:** Reserved matters in the governance framework cannot bypass independent challenge. Letting CEO approval double for board approval without challenge would collapse the governance discipline that distinguishes executive decision-making from constitutional decision-making. The interim arrangement preserves the *form* of the discipline so that when real NEDs arrive, the structure is already in place.

**How to apply:**

- For every decision presented to the CEO, classify it as **CEO** or **BOARD** route, citing the relevant section of the governance framework's Reserved Matters list (§1).
- Default classifications:
  - RAS / RAF and any operational defaults derived from it → **BOARD**.
  - Material policies (capital, liquidity, AML, sanctions, conduct, infosec, privacy, model risk, climate, outsourcing) → **BOARD**.
  - Appointments / removals of executive directors and named designated officers (CRO, CFO, CCO, CISO, CAE, CoSec, IO) → **BOARD**.
  - Strategic plan, budget, capital plan, capital actions above thresholds → **BOARD**.
  - Material acquisitions, disposals, partnerships → **BOARD**.
  - Conflicts and related-party transactions above thresholds → **BOARD**.
  - Sequencing of hires (operational), org-placement of engineers within governance domains, operational sourcing decisions, architectural confirmations → **CEO**.
- For Board items, present a **Board readiness** packet alongside the ask: proposer + peer challenge log + iteration outcome + readiness status.
- The CoSec (Owen) runs the Board-readiness process during the interim period.
- When Marc approves a Board item under the interim arrangement, record the dual-hat status: "approved by CEO on behalf of CEO and independent NEDs (interim)".

title: Chip-vs-background-agent duplication risk — both race, don't spawn both
body:
---
name: Chip-vs-background-agent duplication risk
description: When I spawn_task a chip for Marc to dispatch AND fire a background Agent for the same scope in parallel, both can run and produce duplicate PRs.
type: feedback
originSessionId: b2d802b0-af99-4d8d-ac55-dd5de4d86c13
---
When I use `mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task` to surface a chip Marc can click, the chip runs as an autonomous session in a fresh worktree the moment Marc dispatches it. If I *also* fire a background Agent for the same scope in the same turn, both can run in parallel — producing duplicate PRs (today: PR #14 from Marc's chip-click + PR #15 from my background Agent, both titled "chore: restore CI green on main").

**Why:** Saved 2026-05-08. Wasted ~80k tokens on a redundant CI-fix; required closing one PR with a reconciliation comment to clean up.

**How to apply:** If a chip is already waiting at the start of a turn, do NOT also fire a background Agent for the same scope. Either (a) tell Marc to click the chip and don't fire, (b) fire the Agent inline only if you can verify the chip won't be clicked, or (c) explicitly ask Marc which dispatch path he wants. The chip and background-Agent are not redundant safety nets — they're racing dispatchers, and racing dispatchers cost real tokens.

title: Heavy deterministic ops (runSeed) can exceed default 5s timeout; misattribution via stderr proximity is a trap
body:
---
name: feedback_ci_flake_runseed_timeout_not_worker
description: "The \"(unnamed) ~6s\" Core CI flake was runSeed() tripping the default 5s timeout, NOT the worker-bus-runner crash test; crash-log proximity is coincidental"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 71c0d1c6-f677-4a96-a8e9-825764c5ecaf
---

The intermittent Core-job (`bun run ci:core` → `bun test --isolate`) flake reported as `(unnamed) [~6160ms]` "near worker-crash.ts logs" was **misattributed**. The real failure (from the failed first-attempt Core log) was a NAMED test:
`objective layer — adopted SERVES backfill > re-fold is idempotent … [6804.80ms] ^ this test timed out after 5000ms` in [tests/reg-intelligence-objective-layer.test.ts](prototype/tests/reg-intelligence-objective-layer.test.ts).

**Root cause:** `runSeed()` (full regulatory-objective graph seed) is ~0.9–1.1s idle but CPU+SQLite-bound, so under full-battery contention on a GitHub runner it balloons to ~7s, tripping Bun's **default 5000ms** per-test/hook timeout. That file had SIX runSeed-bearing hooks/tests (a `beforeAll` + three recon-gate `run()`s that each re-seed by design + the idempotency re-fold + advisory-residual gate) and was the lone outlier carrying **no** explicit timeout — the two sibling `*-fold.integration.test.ts` files already use 60_000/120_000 on the identical pattern. Fix (#PR): one `SEED_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` applied to all six. The `(unnamed)` manifestation = the **beforeAll hook** timing out (Bun reports hook timeouts with no test name); the named manifestation = whichever test's runSeed spiked.

**Why:** the worker-bus-runner `worker-crash` stderr appears NEAR the failure only because that file runs adjacent in `--isolate` file-ordering — pure coincidence, not causation.

**How to apply:**
- To find the REAL failing test behind a rerun-passed run, the rerun overwrites the run's conclusion to `success` and hides attempt 1. Pull the failed attempt directly: `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/actions/runs/<id>/attempts/1/jobs` → find the Core job id → `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/actions/jobs/<jobid>/logs`. Grep for `(fail)` / `timed out after`. Don't trust stderr-proximity hypotheses.
- A heavy deterministic op (full seed/fold) tripping the 5s default is right-sized with an explicit `test(fn, 60_000)` / `beforeAll(fn, 60_000)` — that's root-cause, not concealment (a real hang still fails inside 60s). Match the value siblings already use.
- See [[feedback_verify_premise_with_git_lsfiles]] — re-verify the stated premise (here, "it's the worker-bus-runner") against primary evidence before fixing.

title: Session close-out checklist: merge queue, main sync, drift check, dashboard restart, plan refresh
body:
---
name: close session — end-of-session procedure
description: When Marc says "close session", run the full session close-out checklist
type: feedback
originSessionId: 6aa8da4e-8877-4f42-9fbc-8a809d1a708c
---
When Marc says "close session" (or "wrap up" / "end of session"), execute these steps in order:

1. **Merge queue** — `gh pr list --state open` → merge any PRs with green CI (`gh pr checks <n>`); flag any with failing CI.
2. **Main worktree sync** — `git -C /Users/marc/code/Bank merge --ff-only origin/main` (move blocking untracked files aside if needed).
3. **Local drift check** — `git -C /Users/marc/code/Bank status`; surface any uncommitted changes that look like agent output.
4. **Dashboard server check** — `git -C /Users/marc/code/Bank branch --show-current`; if not on `main`, identify the serving process and restart it on main.
5. **Plan-file refresh** — if a `/Users/marc/.claude/plans/*.md` plan file is active for the session's work, update it: status header at top, table of landed PRs, deferred blocks, open F-findings, substrate gaps surfaced. Plans don't auto-refresh; option-2 convention (set 2026-05-16).
6. **Session memory** — write/update the continuation note in memory (what landed, open items, next session checklist).
7. **Session summary** — brief chat report: PRs merged, main at `<sha>`, plan file refreshed, anything left open.

**Why:** Without this, the main worktree drifts behind origin/main (happened today — 11 commits behind), open PRs sit unmerged, and the dashboard serves stale code. A single command avoids all of this.

**How to apply:** Trigger on exact phrase "close session" or close synonyms. "Prod" currently means the local dashboard server (pre-licence, no hosted env yet). Add a deploy step once Azure hosting is active.

title: Domain-correctness lens required beyond CI-green gates for financial outputs
body:
---
name: feedback_controls_guard_type_not_views
description: "Green recon gates prove only what they assert; financial outputs need a domain-correctness lens + a fail-closed control, not just CI-green"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 0bcd110a-e2f4-40ab-9e5e-b7a1b83de8d0
---

The GL trial balance summed USD+ZAR minor units into one `currency:"multi"` row (meaningless — can't add different-currency cents). Marc caught it; the recon suite did not.

**Why the controls missed it:** the currency-safety gates guard the money TYPE and the FOLD — `no-float-money-arithmetic` (floats only, not integer minor-unit sums), `money-codec-no-float`, `account-designated-currency`, `gl-v2-fold-equivalence-fx`/`gl-v2-parity` (posting layer). The bug lived in a derived VIEW (`v2-finance-gl-view.ts`) that had already dropped `Money`→raw `number` minor units with currency hived into a string — escaping the type that makes USD+ZAR impossible, in a blind spot between the type-safety gates (stop at Money) and the fold gates (stop at postings). A `"multi"`/`"mixed"` sentinel is the TELL of a pragmatic flatten (Charter cmd-1/cmd-5 violation). And the unit test CODIFIED the wrong behaviour as expected — a test pointed the wrong way is worse than none.

**Why:** at merge I verified CI-green + structural req + renders, not accounting correctness. Green gates prove only what they assert; they don't prove correctness on dimensions they don't cover. Empty build-phase GL meant no runtime signal either.

**How to apply (standing rule — continual learning without prompting):**
1. On EVERY financial/correctness deliverable close-out, apply the domain lens: does it balance? is it in one currency? does it only sum things that are summable? — don't conflate "the gates I have are green" with "this is correct".
2. Fixing the instance is NOT learning. When a correctness defect is found that a tractable invariant could have caught, MINT or widen a fail-closed recon gate (route to Vera, Internal audit / continuous-assurance engineer — third-line) as part of "done". Lessons → controls → ratchets is the only PROMPT-INDEPENDENT learning; memory + operating rules depend on being reloaded/followed, controls do not.
3. Ban correctness-sentinels (`"multi"`/`"mixed"`/`"various"` for a required dimension) — they mark a flatten that should be a real representation or a tracked gap.

First control minted from this: `recon:gl-currency-dimension-integrity` (Vera) — every GL/trial-balance row carries a real ISO currency; cross-currency rollups only in the functional currency via explicit conversion; no currency sentinel. [[feedback_verify_premise_with_git_lsfiles]] [[project_npa_perspective_ia]]

title: FX tradeId attribution must use source-event provenance, not bare tradeId (same ID can carry both simulated and fixture events)
body:
---
name: feedback_cross_provenance_tradeid_collision
description: "Same FX tradeId can carry both simulated and build-phase-fixture events — attribute by source-event provenance, never bare tradeId"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 70afd455-116b-4640-972c-0461a2077661
---

When analysing the FX sub-ledger, the same `tradeId.value` (e.g. `CONDUCT-TEST-0001`, the SIM-* / 47×-duplicated ids) can carry **both** a `simulated` and a `build-phase-fixture` `FxTradeExecuted` event, plus fixture-lineage settlement/cancellation events. Any filter or attribution keyed on the bare tradeId leaks the wrong lineage in.

**Why:** the GL projection (`gl-projection.ts`) excludes postings whose *source event* is `build-phase-fixture`, but a tradeId-keyed filter pulls in the fixture postings of a colliding id. Folding all reval events for a tradeId, or marking a simulated trade "settled" because a *fixture* SettlementConfirmed shares its id, both produce wrong numbers.

**How to apply:** always attribute postings and derive lifecycle state from the **source event's provenance**, not the tradeId. Map `sourceEventId → (tradeId, provenance)` and only fold events of the target provenance. A simulated trade is "settled"/"cancelled" only if it has a *same-provenance* settlement/cancellation event. See [[project_continuation_2026_06_01_fx_subledger_rebuild]].

title: Dashboard state is always derived from canonical sources, never hand-edited
body:
---
name: Dashboard state is always derived, never hand-edited
description: dashboard-state.json must be re-derived from canonical sources continuously; hand-editing it is forbidden under Principles 1 and 2
type: feedback
originSessionId: ce23d956-757c-4398-9a4d-270747857041
---
The bank dashboard (`prototype/dashboard/`) reads `seeds/dashboard-state.json` as its registry. That file is a **cache / projection** — never a source of truth. It must be continuously re-derived from canonical sources:

- `principles` ← count of Principles in `CLAUDE.md`
- `policies` ← count from `Owner Inbox/2026-05-06_policy-register.md`
- `obligations` ← count from `Regulations/_obligations-register.md`
- `instruments` / `instrumentsAnalysed` ← from `/Regulations/`
- `proceduresPopulated` / `proceduresPlanned` ← from `/Procedures/`
- `ceoDecisionsActioned` ← from the event store (count of `CeoDecision` events)
- `directReports`, `openGovernanceSeats` ← from `/Team/` + Governance Framework
- `decisionsResolved` / `inFlight` ← from event store + Team Inbox state
- `ownerInboxFeed` ← from `/Owner Inbox/*.md` (frontmatter or fallback parse). `decision-required: true` items also lift into `decisionsOpen` (added 2026-05-07; see `feedback_owner_inbox_surfaces_in_dashboard.md`).

**Why:** Principle 1 — only the event log + canonical source documents are authoritative; stored projections (including the dashboard registry) are caches that must be reproducible from canonical sources. Principle 2 (post-2026-05-11 merge) — presentations derive downward from data (rule 2 of the merged single-graph principle); a dashboard is a presentation. Hand-editing the registry creates a presentation-layer fact with no upstream source — exactly what P2 forbids.

**How to apply:**
- Whenever team work changes the bank (new policy, new procedure, new hire, decision actioned, regulation added), do NOT edit `dashboard-state.json` directly. The derivation job must regenerate it.
- Any new metric on the dashboard must declare its canonical source before being added.
- A drift check (derived output vs persisted file) belongs in the recon harness; mismatches are reportable findings.
- The dashboard server should re-derive on startup, on a poll, and on file-watcher events for the canonical paths.

title: Dashboard server holds in-process projection cache across requests; bounce server after event-store mutations
body:
---
name: feedback-dashboard-projection-cache-invalidation
description: Dashboard server caches projection state across requests; new events emitted after server start are NOT picked up until the process is bounced.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6462c70d-5e64-40d1-a099-e4b4591f1320
---

Dashboard server (`prototype/dashboard/server.ts`) holds projection state in process memory across HTTP requests. If new events are appended to the event store after the server boots (backfill scripts, dispatch CLIs, MTM runs), subsequent `/api/*` calls return the *old* projection state until the server is bounced.

**Why:** observed 2026-05-21 during the Product Control realised-P&L fix arc. After PR #694 merged + `bun run backfill:fx-settlement-realised-pnl --force` emitted 14 fresh `SettlementRealisedPnlCorrected` events, `/api/product-control/daily-pnl` kept returning the pre-backfill numbers (ZAR +201m bogus realised) for multiple curl calls. Restarting the dashboard (`kill <PID>` + `bun run prototype/dashboard/server.ts`) immediately returned the corrected numbers (ZAR +7.65m). Same store, same projection code, different process — proof of in-process caching.

**How to apply:**
- Whenever a backfill / direct event-store mutation / scheduled handler runs after the dashboard is up, **bounce the dashboard** before verifying via `/api/*`.
- A `curl` returning stale data is NOT proof the fix didn't land; verify by inspecting the event store directly (`sqlite3 ... SELECT ... FROM events`) before concluding the projection is wrong.
- Substrate fix: either (a) projections rebuild on each request (cost: replay every time), (b) projections subscribe to event-store append hooks and invalidate, (c) SSE/websocket invalidation channel. Worth a Vera or substrate brief; not addressed today.
- Related: dashboard server defaults to cwd-relative `.local/event.db` if `BANK_EVENT_DB` isn't set — pair this rule with [[feedback_dashboard_cwd_relative_db_path]] when restarting.

title: dashboard-state.json must not embed local-only .local/event.db events
body:
---
name: dashboard-state.json must not depend on local .local/event.db
description: Committing a regen of dashboard-state.json that includes T-stamped resolved decisions sourced from local-only .local/event.db breaks CI — CI has no .local, so derivation produces fewer decisions and the dashboard-derivation recon flags drift.
type: feedback
originSessionId: d016ed09-1a32-49a1-ab63-2475581d5479
---
When committing dashboard-state.json regen, never include T-stamped resolved decisions sourced from local-only `.local/event.db`. CI runners have no `.local/`, so their derivation produces only the historical (date-only `actionedAt`) decisions from `dashboard-curated.json`. Cache says 25, derivation produces 6 → drift fail.

**Why:** observed 2026-05-09 on PR #136 — CI failed twice with `dashboard-derivation-reconciliation` drift on `decisionsResolved`/`bank.metrics.ceoDecisionsActioned`. The events were emitted to `<worktree>/.local/event.db` (gitignored). Regen captured local state. Push committed mismatch. CI failed. Fix: revert dashboard-state.json to main's version (which only carries the 6 historical from curated), let CI's empty-store derivation match.

**How to apply:**
- After running `recordCeoDecision` or any backfill that writes to `.local/event.db`, do NOT regen dashboard-state.json into the PR. The cache should only ever reflect `decisionsResolvedSeed` (historical, no T-stamp).
- If you do regen for local development, drop the change from your commit (`git checkout origin/main -- prototype/seeds/dashboard-state.json` before staging).
- Long-term substrate fix: dashboard-state.json should either (a) not be committed to git at all (treat as runtime cache), or (b) regen should only emit historical-shape entries, ignoring `.local` events. Until then this is a manual discipline.
- Companion: `.local/event.db` is cwd-relative — running scripts from worktree-root vs `prototype/` produces different stores. Use `prototype/.local/event.db` consistently if you must inspect.

title: Dashboards live (event-driven); reports as-of-date (immutable snapshots)
body:
---
name: Dashboards live; reports as-of-date
description: Dashboards must update live (event-driven, no stale seeds, no polling intervals). Reports are point-in-time as-of-date artefacts (immutable snapshots with the as-of timestamp baked in).
type: feedback
originSessionId: 612ad370-3e15-44b5-a5d0-d38ed473a20c
---
The two artefact-types serve different epistemic roles and must be implemented differently.

**Dashboards = LIVE.** A dashboard surfaces the *current* state of the bank — when the user looks at it, the data on screen reflects current canonical state, not a stale snapshot. **Periodic refresh is acceptable. User-triggered refresh is acceptable.** What is *not* acceptable is a refresh that doesn't actually re-derive from canonical sources (i.e. periodic re-reads of an unchanging cache file). Event-driven push (SSE / WebSocket) is one valid implementation but not required — periodic re-derivation on a sensible cadence (seconds-to-minutes), plus a user-triggered "refresh now" affordance, both meet the bar so long as the refresh actually re-queries the canonical sources / event log.

**Reports = AS-OF-DATE.** A report is an immutable point-in-time artefact. Its as-of timestamp is its identity. Reading the same report a year later returns the same data — because it's a snapshot of what the event log said at that as-of date (per Principle 1's "as-of replay is a first-class capability"). Reports are generated, signed, and frozen; they do not auto-update.

**Why:** Marc set this rule on 2026-05-09 after observing that the current dashboards (started via `bun run dashboard`) consume `prototype/seeds/dashboard-state.json` — a derived cache that only re-runs when `recon:dashboard` re-runs. The `refreshMs: 30000` interval polls the cache, not the event log. That makes the "dashboard" a periodically-refreshed report, not a dashboard. The asymmetry must be corrected: live-ness is the dashboard's defining property, as-of-date-ness is the report's.

**How to apply:**
- Any artefact named `*-dashboard` or surfaced under `/dashboard/*` must be event-driven. No `seeds/` consumption at runtime; no scheduled-refresh contracts. Event-source pushes; UI subscribes.
- Any artefact named `*-report` or surfaced as a generated PDF / HTML / XML must carry an explicit `asOf` field, must be immutable once generated, and must be reproducible from the event log at any future point (per Principle 1's as-of-replay).
- The current `seeds/dashboard-state.json` is a substrate gap, not a feature. It should be retired in favour of an event-log-backed live projection layer (Anya, Data / analytics engineer; substrate-side Atlas, Core banking platform architect).
- BA returns, financial statements, STRs, FATCA / CRS XML, board packs, audit reports — all reports. Live activity feeds, decisions queues, escalation inboxes, fleet status, agent state, obligations register state — all dashboards.
- Dashboards may render *historical* data (e.g. "trade volume by day for the last 30 days") — that's fine; the live property is that the renderer subscribes to new events and updates the chart as they land. Polling at 30s intervals is not live-ness; it's slow polling.

title: Decision approvals must target shared event store, not worktree-local store
body:
---
name: feedback_decision_approve_shared_store
description: "Decision-approval scripts must target the shared canonical event store, else approvals land in a worktree-local store and the dashboard shows them perpetually open"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 469872fa-15f9-44cc-9f67-5f41b513c151
---

`platform/composition.ts` resolves `eventStore` with `resolveEventDbPath({ excludeHomeDefault: true })`. So any decision script (requestDecision / recordDecision) run **without** `BANK_EVENT_DB` set writes to the per-worktree `.local/event.db`, NOT the shared canonical store the dashboard reads (`$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`).

**Why:** A 2026-05-17 approval of D-RMS-PHASE-2 / D-RMS-PHASE-3 (`scripts/approve-phase-2-3.ts`) landed the `approved` events in a worktree-local store. A later `backfill:decisions-framework-cutover` synthesised `requested` openers into the shared store, but the approvals stayed stranded local → canonical store showed only `requested` → decisions appeared open forever. Re-approving via UI/script normally hit the local store again (stale-skip or validation error), so it never stuck — Marc reported "I get an error when I try to approve."

**How to apply:** To approve/close a decision so the dashboard reflects it, always run:
`BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db bun run scripts/<approve-script>.ts`
Then verify with `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db bun run scripts/check-open-decisions.ts` → expect the id gone from the open list. Same rule as dispatch CLIs (cross-worktree event-store sync). [[feedback_merged_is_not_canonical]]

title: Decision events must carry substantive backing rationale and key facts, not just the outcome
body:
---
name: feedback_decision_backing_information
description: "Decisions in the event store must include the backing information that was presented to arrive at the decision, not just the decision itself"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: fbebeb63-2bdf-463e-857a-d440316df3fe
---

Every `Decision` event (and any `recordDecision` call) must carry the backing information that was presented to Marc to arrive at that decision — not just the outcome.

**Why:** The event store is the single source of truth (Principle 1). A bare decision event without the supporting rationale, data, and analysis cannot be reconstructed or audited after the fact. The backing information is part of the decision artefact, not a separate document.

**How to apply:** When calling `recordDecision`, populate `rationale` with the substantive reasoning and key facts that informed the decision. If quantitative analysis, options comparison, or risk assessment was presented, summarise it inline or reference it via `sourceDocHashes`/`citations`. A `Decision(approved)` event that contains only a title and a phase is incomplete — Vera (internal audit) and any future governance review must be able to reconstruct the decision context from the event alone.

title: Backfill-only decisions are invisible to production replay; require scrooge:session-delegation pairing

description: How to identify and fix decisions that only exist in prose/backfill events; future consistency rule

originSessionId: 76a50c44-f3a7-4e9c-87a5-8a43b1d297af

- Script at `prototype/scripts/record-gap-decisions.ts` shows the pattern

title: CEO decision approval requires dual write: record + event emission
body:
---
name: Approving a decision in markdown without emitting the CeoDecision event creates a ghost-open dashboard state
description: Every CEO decision that gets approved+actioned via PR merge must also emit a typed `CeoDecision(approve)` event. The dashboard projection treats absent events as "still open" — code merge alone never resolves the decision.
type: feedback
originSessionId: d999a4c7-4726-4a70-bd68-d230c7d40baa
---
When a CEO decision is approved (markdown record + code PR merged), a `CeoDecision` event with `action="approve"` **must also be emitted** against the `decisionId`, dated when the decision was effectively made. Without the event, the dashboard's `decisionsOpen` projection keeps surfacing the decision and Marc gets "asked the same question repeatedly."

**Why:** On 2026-05-11, `D-PRINCIPLES-P2-P6-MERGE` was approved by Marc and actioned via PR #214 (spec), PR #215 (the actual principles-merge code change), PR #216 (cross-ref fixup). All three merged on `main` on 2026-05-11. But no `CeoDecision` event was ever emitted against the `decisionId`. The dashboard's `derive.ts::reduceCeoDecisions` only resolves a decision when it sees a non-`request-revision` event in the store — the markdown merge alone tells the projection nothing. The decision stayed visible in `decisionsOpen` until I back-recorded the event with the script at `prototype/scripts/close-out-ceo-decisions-2026-05-11.ts`.

A separate but related instance: `D-MARKETS-CAPITAL-TIME-SHAPE` had a stale `request-revision` event from 2026-05-07 that was a Scrooge smoke-test of `/api/decide`, mis-attributed to Marc because the form hardcodes `actor="marc@tgv.co.za"`. Latest-wins-per-key meant that smoke-test event kept the decision in a fake "reopened" state. The symmetry isn't just "events follow records" — it's also "events have correct actor attribution."

**How to apply:**
- Treat decision approval as a two-step write: (1) merge the action PR, (2) emit `CeoDecision(approve)` with the merge timestamp and Marc as actor. Use the helper at `prototype/runtime/decisions/record.ts::recordCeoDecision` rather than constructing the event by hand.
- When emitting an approve event back-dated to a prior PR, set `asOf = <PR mergedAt>` so the audit trail is honest.
- If the dashboard shows a decision as `(reopened)` but you don't remember reopening it, check the latest `CeoDecision` event for that ID and its `actor`. A stale smoke-test event with `actor.id="marc@tgv.co.za"` and a non-business hour timestamp is the smell.
- One-shot corrections: write an idempotent script under `prototype/scripts/` that checks for the event via `existingDecisionKeys` (pattern in `runtime/decisions/backfill-from-records.ts`) before emitting. Re-running is then a no-op.
- Operational follow-up after merging the script's PR: run the script against the canonical / production event store. The local `.local/event.db` in the dispatched worktree is throw-away; the running dashboard reads from wherever the deployed server's store lives.
- Substrate gap (not closed today): a Vera recon `decision-record-event-symmetry` would assert that every Owner-Inbox decision record marked approved has a backing `CeoDecision(approve)` event, and vice versa. Pair with an `/api/decide` identity seam so future smoke-tests can't mis-attribute to Marc.

This is the strongest practical demonstration so far of why Principle 1 (events are truth) is load-bearing: the dashboard cannot reason about decision state from the markdown alone, no matter how clean the records are.

title: Dispatched agents cannot access gitignored repo-relative secrets; use fixed absolute path ~/.config/bank/.env

metadata:

**Rule:** never reference a gitignored repo-relative path (e.g. `prototype/.env.local`) in a dispatch brief — the dispatched agent's isolated worktree won't have the file. Secrets live at `~/.config/bank/.env` (mode 600); briefs reference that absolute path and instruct the agent's loader (python-dotenv / dotenv-cli) to read from there.

**Why:** 2026-05-21 Atlas dispatch for the Graphiti spike. I put the Anthropic key at `<my-worktree>/prototype/.env.local` and told Atlas the key was at `prototype/.env.local`. Atlas was in a different worktree (`agent-aea39df698bd02b9f`); gitignored files don't cross worktrees, so the file wasn't there. Atlas's loader either found an empty/missing key or read a stale value; result was a 401 from Anthropic. The LLM-extraction tier — Graphiti's actual value-add — never ran, which made the spike unable to test the bitemporal claim either. The whole D-KG-GRAPHITI-ADOPT decision was made on incomplete evidence because of this dispatch mistake. Marc's chosen fix (2026-05-21): machine-wide secrets at `~/.config/bank/.env`.

**How to apply:** in every dispatch brief that involves an agent calling out to an LLM / API: (a) cite the absolute path `~/.config/bank/.env`, never a repo-relative path; (b) instruct the agent to verify the file exists + non-empty before starting work, and fail-fast with a clear error if it doesn't; (c) if the brief involves a new secret type not already in `~/.config/bank/.env`, ask Marc to add it before dispatching, don't paste it in chat (see [[macos-smart-quotes]] for credential-in-chat lessons). Related: [[agent-worktree-isolation]] — same root structural pattern (isolated worktrees don't carry untracked files); this is its credentials-specific corollary.

title: SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ with stale WAL sidecar; recover via delete -shm/-wal when WAL is 0 bytes
body:
---
name: feedback-event-store-wal-sidecar-recovery
description: "SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ on the canonical event.db = stale WAL sidecar, not disk/corruption; recover by bouncing the writer + deleting -shm/-wal (when WAL is 0 bytes)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ce76de37-ee03-468a-8da1-9a05e6807ec8
---

On 2026-06-13 the canonical event store (`$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`) threw `SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ` on EVERY new connection (store.ts:417, at `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) — both ad-hoc `sqlite3`/`bun:sqlite` readers AND the app's dispatch CLIs. Event-write path (dispatch lifecycle, decision records, recon) fully blocked. The long-running dashboard (then PID 15357, open ~17h) kept working because it built its WAL index while the store was healthy; only NEW openers failed.

**Misleading first hypothesis:** `df` showed 97% / 13 GiB free → looked like disk pressure. It wasn't. Freeing ~1.8 GB of old `event.db.bak-*`/`.pre-*` snapshots did NOT clear it (and APFS didn't even reflect the free immediately — local snapshot retention; `df` rounding hides sub-GB moves on a 460 GB volume).

**Decisive non-destructive diagnosis:** `cp event.db /tmp/probe.db` (copy has NO sidecar) then `sqlite3 /tmp/probe.db "PRAGMA integrity_check; SELECT COUNT(*)"` → **`ok`, 106,020 events**. Plus `dd … bs=1m count=500` wrote fine → disk genuinely fine. ∴ main DB healthy + disk fine ⇒ the fault is the **stale `-shm` WAL-index sidecar** (its mtime lagged the main DB; WAL itself was 0 bytes = already checkpointed, so NO uncommitted data at risk). (Note: `bun:sqlite` gave a spurious `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` on the copy where the `sqlite3` CLI opened it fine — trust the CLI.)

**Recovery (CEO-approved, the standard fix):** stop the writer holding the DB (the dashboard) → confirm `lsof event.db` shows no holders → `rm -f event.db-shm event.db-wal` (safe ONLY because WAL was 0 bytes / checkpointed and main DB integrity-checks ok) → reopen via the app path (SQLite rebuilds the sidecar clean; a dispatch start-run wrote `ok:true`, WAL rebuilt to ~251 KB) → restart the dashboard (`BANK_EVENT_DB=… nohup bun run dashboard/server.ts &`, :3010 → HTTP 302).

**How to apply:**
- `SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ` on a store that a long-lived process is already using = suspect the stale WAL sidecar FIRST, not corruption. Confirm with a sidecar-less copy + integrity_check before touching anything.
- NEVER delete `-shm`/`-wal` while a process holds the DB (corruption risk). Stop the writer first; verify with `lsof`. Only safe to delete the WAL when it's 0 bytes (checkpointed) — otherwise checkpoint first or you lose uncommitted writes.
- Deliverables on `main`/git are unaffected by an event-store availability incident; only the at-the-moment event writes are. Reconstruct lifecycle events from briefs/PRs if needed.
- Surfaced to Marc as a decision-required incident (didn't take destructive action on the canonical store / didn't bounce a 17h process without OK). [[feedback_surface_decisions_proactively]] [[feedback_verify_premise_with_git_lsfiles]]

title: Two event stores — shared ($HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db) for dispatch/dashboard; local (.local/event.db) for CI/recon
body:
---
name: feedback_event_store_wrong_path
description: Two event stores — shared store for dispatch+dashboard; local store for CI+recon; correct prefix depends on context
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7d3b4eae-a274-4c02-8814-ad855a93eda0
---

There are TWO event stores in production:
1. **Shared store** (`$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`, ~190k events): used by dispatch CLI, dashboard server, cross-worktree sync.
2. **Local store** (`prototype/.local/event.db`, ~438k events): used by CI, recon scripts (e.g. `decision-record-event-symmetry` hardcodes this path), test runs, backfill scripts.

**Dispatch CLI** (open-brief, start-run, close-run): always prefix `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`.

**recordDecision() / general event emission (recon-visible)**: do NOT prefix. Let composition resolve to local store. The recon scripts read the local store and won't see events emitted to the shared store. Events emitted without BANK_EVENT_DB land in the local store (composition fallback = `.local/event.db`).

**Dashboard-visible events** (RecordFiled, AgentBriefIssued, etc.): prefix with `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db` to land in shared store that dashboard reads.

**Why:** This dual-store architecture exists because CI uses the local store (no `$HOME` available in runners), while the dashboard and dispatch CLI need a cross-worktree-stable path. The `decision-record-event-symmetry` recon hardcodes `prototype/.local/event.db` and ignores `BANK_EVENT_DB` entirely.

**How to apply:** When running `recordDecision()` for recon compliance (to clear `decision-record-event-symmetry` advisory warnings), run from `prototype/` without any env override. When running dispatch CLI operations, always prefix with `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`.

title: FX cancellation GL posting omits PrincipalPayment reversals; manual correcting journals required
body:
---
name: feedback_fx_cancel_prin_reversal_pattern
description: "When cancelling an FX trade that had PrincipalPayment GL entries pre-processed, the cancellation posting leaves spurious balances — must post correcting cancellation-reversal journals"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: aa3d48ee-c112-4f86-9bc0-bbd6bc499e2e
---

`fxCancellationJournals` (PR-FX-CANCEL) only reverses the original `FxTradeExecuted` booking legs. It does not detect or reverse `PrincipalPayment` GL entries (PR-FX-PRIN) that were already posted for the same trade.

**Why:** The sim pre-emits future-dated `PrincipalPayment` events at booking time; the GL engine processes them immediately (no `as_of` bound). A subsequent cancellation then over-debits payable accounts and over-credits receivable accounts.

**Substrate gap:** `alert:integrity:fx-cancel-prin-no-reversal` filed 2026-06-01. Proper fix: cancellation handler in `gl-posting-engine.ts` must query existing `SubLedgerPostingEmitted{postingType:"fx-principal-payment"}` for the trade and include their reversals.

**How to apply:** After any FX trade cancellation, check the payable and receivable accounts for that trade's currencies. If a spurious debit (payable) or credit (receivable) appears, post two `cancellation-reversal` SubLedgerPostingEmitted entries mirroring the original PR-FX-PRIN legs in reverse:
- Deliver leg reversal: Dr Nostro / Cr Payable
- Receive leg reversal: Dr Receivable / Cr Nostro

Amount comes from the `PrincipalPayment` event's `|netCash|`. Use `nostroAccountFor(ccy)` mapping: ZAR→ACC-1200-001, USD→ACC-1200-002, EUR→ACC-1200-003, others→ACC-1200-002 (default).

title: GitHub Actions concurrency.group must scope per-workflow; shared groups cancel queued runs
body:
---
name: GitHub Actions concurrency.group — per-workflow, never shared
description: For an agent fleet, each workflow's concurrency.group must scope to itself; shared groups cancel queued runs because effective queue depth is 1
type: feedback
originSessionId: 5eed9e6f-937e-44f3-b385-9695f2a0ace7
---
**Set 2026-05-07** after the agent runtime's first multi-agent dispatch surfaced this.

## The rule

Every agent-runtime workflow under `.github/workflows/agent-runtime-*.yml` declares:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

**Never** use a shared group like `agent-autocommit` across multiple workflows in the agent fleet, even if the intent is to serialise pushes to `main`.

## What's wrong with shared groups

GitHub Actions `concurrency.group` with `cancel-in-progress: false` has an effective queue depth of **1**. When a third dispatch arrives while a run is in-progress and another is queued, GitHub *cancels the queued run* in favour of the new one — only the in-progress and the most-recently-queued runs survive.

Today's evidence: dispatching Anya, Scrooge, Owen, Mira, Senna in quick succession with `group: agent-autocommit` produced:

- Anya — ran (in-progress when others arrived).
- Scrooge — queued, then cancelled when Owen arrived.
- Owen — queued, then cancelled when Mira arrived.
- Mira — queued, then cancelled when Senna arrived.
- Senna — ran (was the most-recently-queued when Anya finished).

Three of five autonomous-runs lost; not at all what the shared group was meant to do.

## What per-workflow groups do correctly

`group: ${{ github.workflow }}` scopes the group to one workflow file. So:

- Vera vs Vera: queues / cancels (single workflow protects itself from re-entry on rapid dispatches).
- Vera vs Atlas: independent — both run in parallel on schedule.
- Push race between Vera and Atlas is handled by the push-retry loop (`feedback_agent_autocommit_race.md`), not by a workflow-level lock.

## Triggering rule

Whenever a new agent workflow is added under `.github/workflows/agent-runtime-*.yml`, it MUST use:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

If a future need actually requires global serialisation (e.g. all agents must produce events through a single ingest), that's a substrate change — model it explicitly, not as a workflow-level lock.
