title: FX cancellation must emit GL reversals within the SAME provenance partition as opening; bare cancel-flag doesn't empty GL
body:
---
name: project_fx_cancel_gl_reversal
description: "FX trade cancel must REVERSE GL postings, not just flag the instrument cancelled —"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5d7c8577-e5fa-4703-a5fa-61d9fecc55c4
---

**D-FX-FIXTURE-PROVENANCE-CANCEL-AND-HARDEN** (CEO 2026-06-22). Arc: "list all trades" → 4 FX fixtures wrongly tagged `production` → cancel (don't reclassify) → GL still showed trade balances.

**Root cause of the mis-tag:** `scripts/backfill-fil-instances.ts` appended `FilInstrumentCreated` with NO provenance → `EventStore.resolveProvenanceForAppend` → `defaultProvenanceFor(type)`; `FilInstrumentCreated` hardcoded category `governance`=`production` in `provenance-category.ts`. Polymorphic instrument carrier (real capital + fixtures) → type-keyed default **fails open to production**.

**★Cancel ≠ accounting reversal (the load-bearing lesson).** Appending `FilInstrumentTerminated{cancelled}` flips instrument status but does NOT empty the GL. The V2 GL trial balance (`computeTrialBalanceV2Uncached` → `foldFxContributionLegs`) is a pure fold: `FilInstrumentCreated` posts opening legs; a bare `cancelled` termination fired `PR-FX-CLOSE-V2` (`postFxCloseLegs`) which posted **Dr 0 / Cr 0 memo** — never reversed the opening legs. Two compounding causes: (1) zero-memo close rule; (2) **provenance-lens mismatch** — cancellations tagged `build-phase-fixture` while creations tagged `production`, so under the GL `production-only` lens the cancels are filtered OUT and never fold. **A reversal must net within the SAME provenance partition as the creation it reverses.**

**Fix (#1510, MERGED `e8815482`):** new born-V2 `PR-FX-CANCEL-REVERSAL-V2` (`postFxCancellationReversalLegs` in `v2-core/posting-rules/fx.ts`). FX fold scans terminated stream WITHOUT the provenance filter for bare cancellations, reverses exactly the opening legs that folded under the active lens (decoupled from cancel event's own tag), idempotent (once per instance). Settled-with-reval derecognition preserved byte-for-byte. `recon:gl-v2-fold-equivalence-fx` golden updated. Data reconciled via `scripts/reconcile-fx-fixture-cancellation-completeness.ts` (idempotent). Result: 0 FX rows under both lenses; R300m capital intact under +Sim. Ratchet HELD 286.

**★Verify at the layer the user sees.** I claimed "book empty" after checking instrument STATUS (0 live positions) but the GL still showed balances — must verify the actual projection. **And: a data fix that depends on a CODE fold change won't show until the code merges + dashboard redeploys** — verifying with MY worktree's OLD fold showed FX rows still there; had to run the PR branch's code against the shared store to see 0. Dashboard `.dashboard-live` auto-pulls origin/main ~30s and kickstarts the bun server, so live GL cleared shortly after merge.

**OUTSTANDING follow-on:** the fail-closed provenance harden (make untagged FIL-instance-carrier appends hard-reject instead of defaulting to production) — its run DIED mid-work (blocked); still approved under the same decision; not yet landed.

title: FX trade-date FVTPL recognition + off-balance-sheet memorandum (PR #1534/1536/1538) — settlement clean end-to-end; realised only on FCY→ZAR conversion
body:
---
name: project_fx_trade_date_fvtpl_obs
description: FX trade-date IFRS recognition fix — FVTPL + off-balance-sheet memorandum (PR
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: cebd204f-5165-4acb-9046-ef13871aa9df
---

**D-FX-TRADE-DATE-FVTPL-OBS — PR [#1534](https://github.com/marchouze/scrooge/pull/1534) MERGED 2026-06-24.** Fixed a real FX trade-date GL accounting bug, surfaced when the live FX V2 simulator ([[project_fx_v2_live_simulator]]) generated GBP/ZAR trades and the CEO noticed a GBP asset AND GBP liability being raised.

**The bug:** `v2-core/posting-rules/fx.ts` `postFxInitialRecognitionLegs` (`PR-FX-001-V2`) booked a SAME-currency Dr-receivable / Cr-payable pair, both = the base notional (mapped risk-style single-notional+direction onto a GL pair). It nets to zero, records no position, drops the counter-currency, ignores the `fxAgreement` quad, and inflates BA-100 gross assets/liabilities.

**The fix (CEO chose Policy A of two — FVTPL — + reflect OBS notionals in the TB):**
- Trade date ON-balance-sheet: IFRS 9 FVTPL derivative at fair value ≈ 0 at inception → **no on-BS gross-up**. Position carried by daily reval MtM.
- `PR-FX-REVAL-V2` now posts the fair-value **DELTA** (`fairValueDeltaSinceLastMeasurement`, born-V2 additive optional on economicTerms), not the full notional; absent delta → zero memo. (Reval is dark — no FilInstrumentAmended emitted — so forward-correctness.)
- Trade date OFF-balance-sheet: contractual buy/sell notionals → new memorandum accounts **ACC-9100-001/002/003** (category `memorandum-off-balance-sheet-fx-commitment`), **self-balancing per currency** from the quad: BUY(Cb,Ab)→Dr 9100-001[Cb]/Cr 9100-003[Cb]; SELL(Cs,As)→Dr 9100-003[Cs]/Cr 9100-002[Cs]. Reflected in the TB in a segregated OBS section, EXCLUDED from on-BS asset/liability/equity tiles, the in-balance check, and BA-100 on-BS lines.
- New `off-balance-sheet` GlClass in `dashboard/v2-finance-gl-view.ts`; BA-100 (`ba-100-balance-sheet.ts`) fail-closed if an OBS account maps to an on-BS section.
- New ENFORCING `recon:fx-trade-date-obs-memorandum`: asserts zero on-BS (ACC-2100-*) legs at trade date + all legs on OBS (ACC-9100-*) spanning the two quad currencies, self-balancing per ccy. (gl-v2-fold-equivalence-fx can't catch a consistent-but-wrong rule — both used the same bad rule.)

**SETTLEMENT-SIDE COMPLETION — PR [#1536](https://github.com/marchouze/scrooge/pull/1536) MERGED 2026-06-24** (same decision, no new one — completes Policy A). #1534 fixed trade-date only; settlement still relieved a gross FX receivable/payable that trade-date no longer created → settled trades left DANGLING inverted ACC-2100-002/003 + un-released OBS. Fix: FVTPL settlement recognises cash at settled amount + balances with **realised FX P&L (ACC-2100-006)** per currency (never touches receivable/payable); new **PR-FX-OBS-RELEASE-V2** reverses the trade-date ACC-9100-* OBS legs on settled/matured termination (open trades keep commitment; cancel still nets via existing reversal); native GL in-balance check now sums **per-currency**. New ENFORCING `recon:fx-settlement-fvtpl-integrity` (fully-settled ⇒ zero on-BS receivable/payable AND zero residual OBS; open ⇒ OBS kept). Verified on live sim book: post-settlement ACC-2100/ACC-9100 all net to zero, cash+realised-P&L recognised, TB balances. So a settled FX trade is now clean end-to-end.

**P&L MODEL CORRECTION — PR #1538 MERGED 2026-06-25** (D-FX-PNL-FCY-EXPOSURE-REVALUATION, refines the above). ★CEO's accounting steer: FX P&L = change in ZAR value of the FCY EXPOSURE (cost-basis); UNREALISED while open — and the exposure stays open ACROSS settlement (a forward receivable becoming cash is a change of FORM, same ccy/amount/cost-basis, NOT realisation). Settled FCY cash is revalued IDENTICALLY to an unsettled contract. REALISED only on FCY→ZAR conversion (squaring). So #1536's "realised P&L on settlement" was WRONG twice over. Fix: settlement now P&L-NEUTRAL (cash vs born-V2 clearing acct ACC-2100-027, never realised-P&L ACC-2100-006); settled cash carries `zarCostBasis` (born-V2 optional on cash economicTerms; = booked ZAR of the FCY leg); cohort/daily P&L engine WIDENED to revalue settled FCY cash (no longer dropped when the trade terminates); new `PR-FX-CONVERT-V2` realisation rule (proceeds − cost basis, reclassify unrealised→realised); recon:fx-pnl-fcy-exposure-integrity ENFORCING (ACC-2100-006 reached only via convert/derecog). Worked example USD7m@18.565→spot19.00 = +R3.045m IDENTICAL for open forward and settled cash (test-proven). FCY→ZAR convert rule is forward-correctness (sim doesn't convert yet). ★LESSON: realised vs unrealised boundary is the EXPOSURE's conversion to functional ccy, not the trade's settlement; a P&L account must never hold a FCY balance (use a clearing acct that nets to ~0 in reporting).

★KEY LESSONS:
- **FX posting logic is duplicated in 3+ places kept byte-equivalent by recon:** the `v2-core/posting-rules/fx.ts` fold, the `gl-posting-engine-v2.ts` emitter, and `posting-rules-v2/fx-fold.ts`/`fx-instance-fold.ts`. Any FX-posting change must touch all + rebaseline `recon:gl-v2-fold-equivalence-fx`. (Here byte-equiv held by construction — all delegate to the same lifted pure fns.)
- **Risk reads FIL instances, GL reads legs — independent axes.** SA-CCR/BA-320 read `platform/risk/sa-ccr/fil-instance-positions.ts` (notional+direction), NOT GL legs, so a GL posting bug does NOT misstate FX RWA/EAD. BA-100 balance sheet DOES read the trial balance, so a GL gross-up inflates it.
- **Settlement was already correct** (`settle-fx-leg.ts` materialises the two cash legs in their own currencies); only trade-date recognition was wrong — trade-date is now OBS-only so no double-count.
- **For trading-book FX, FVTPL (derivative, nil-at-inception) is the textbook IFRS 9 treatment** — not gross receivable/payable. Gross regular-way (Policy B) needs reporting-ccy accounting to balance multi-currency.
- Process: analysis-doc first → recordDecision (session-delegation, `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/...` for canonical store) → events-first dispatch to Bea (open-brief AgentBriefIssued → background Agent worktree → start-run → close-run with `--pr <url>` not `--deliverable`; `--expected` kind = `code-pr` not `pr`).

title: FX vanilla settlement model refactored: N uniform TradeSettlementExecuted events per trade, not 2-leg FilFxSettlementConfirmed
body:
---
name: project_fx_trade_settlement_product_model
description: "FX vanilla Trade/Settlement/Product model — settlement = N uniform single-asset TradeSettlementExecuted events at cost, not a 2-leg event. 3 PRs MERGED 2026-06-23."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

**D-FX-TRADE-SETTLEMENT-PRODUCT-MODEL** (CEO-approved 2026-06-23, session-delegation). Reference implementation on FX vanilla; bonds/repo adopt later.

**The model (CEO):** a settlement is a UNIFORM SINGLE-ASSET movement — "holding H ↑/↓ by amount A at cost C, executing trade T" — NOT a bespoke 2-leg FX event. Three constructs: (1) **Trade = the agreement** (`FilInstrumentCreated`, executory receivable/payable); (2) **Settlement = the execution** — N uniform `TradeSettlementExecuted` events (FX spot = 2: received-cash + paid-cash), each carrying booked-vs-settled so derecognition + realised P&L (IAS 21 §28) fall out per movement; effect = create/adjust a holding (cash now, any asset class later) AT COST; (3) **Product = the glue** — type-level rulebook + per-trade `tradeFamily` grouping (Create + Settles + holdings under the trade id). Dissolves the FX-specific `FilFxSettlementConfirmed` (2-leg/near-far/bought-sold).

**3 PRs MERGED 2026-06-23 (staged, byte-stable):**
- #1516 (Slice 1) — born-V2 `TradeSettlementExecuted` (`v2-core/fil-instances/trade-settlement.ts`; fields tradeInstance/holdingInstance/holdingType/holdingAssetClass/movement/bookedCarrying/cost), `decomposeFxSettlementToTradeSettlements`, `buildSettledHoldingPayload` (holding-at-cost), `postTradeSettlementLegs` reusing an extracted shared `postSettlementMovementLegs` primitive. DARK + byte-proven == FilFxSettlementConfirmed (gain+loss). v2status v2-parallel.
- #1517 (Slice 2) — `TradeSettlementExecuted` is now the explicit settlement-of-record emitted at the production settlement seam (`materialise-settled-cash.ts` + `settle-fx-leg.ts`); `deriveFxInstanceLegs` consumes it + historical FilFxSettlementConfirmed (dual-read, both via shared primitive); `tradeFamily`/`foldTradeFamilies` grouping read-model. Trial balance unchanged. ★PREMISE CORRECTION: FX vanilla NEVER emitted FilFxSettlementConfirmed in production (0 in store) — settlement was implicit (terminated{settled}+cash); the 2-leg event was dormant/oracle. So the cutover is ADDITIVE (makes settlement explicit), not a replace; historical backfill opts out (emitSettlementEvents:false) to keep the fixture byte-stable.
- #1518 (Slice 3) — FX OTC vanilla NPA updated EVENTS-FIRST: refined `ProductConceptualised` (lifecycle family lists TradeSettlementExecuted as settlement-of-record, FilFxSettlementConfirmed retired/oracle), `ProductPostApprovalFinding` PAF-FX-SETTLEMENT-MODEL-001 closed by `ProductDimensionRetrospectiveReview` (accounting dim, reviewedBy Bea); consolidated render §5/§6.

**Ratchet HELD 286 across all 3; born-V2, no new V1 import.**

**OPEN follow-on (tracked):** BoP deferred gap `fx-bop-projection-trade-settlement-source` (conduct dim, licence-day-gated) — `finsurv-bop-projection.ts` reads only FilFxSettlementConfirmed/FilNdfFixingObserved; must also fold TradeSettlementExecuted when BoP per-transaction reporting activates at licence-day. Also still open from the prior arc: the fail-closed FIL provenance harden (D-FX-FIXTURE-PROVENANCE-CANCEL-AND-HARDEN, run died).

GOTCHA: dispatch:start-run does NOT validate the briefId exists — I passed a wrong-slug briefId (guessed from the brief heading, not the open-brief-returned title slug) and it silently linked an orphan run; fix = withdraw orphan + start-run with the exact returned briefId. The driver (simulator-side) constructs the tag, not the SUT (Rule B intent intact).
- **Two CI carve-outs every new sim-emitter/test needs:** (1) `EXPLICIT_PROVENANCE_ALLOWLIST` in `platform/recon/provenance-emit-discipline.ts` for any file calling `simulatedTag(...)`; (2) `CONSTRUCTION_CARVE_OUT_FILES` in `platform/recon/permission-gate-default.ts` for test files using raw `new EventStore(":memory:")`. title: Agent goal-loops require three-way coherence: §9 label ∈ decisionsInScope, plannedEvent ⊆ §11 eventsEmitted, handler actually emits it; mismatch silently jams or defers
body:
---
name: project_goal_loop_three_way_coherence
description: Agent goal-loop derivers require three-way event coherence; a mismatch silently jams or defers the loop
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 02a983be-5eac-40eb-bcc4-47c1521a7d84
---

A cohort goal-loop deriver (`runtime/agents/<agent>-goal-loop.ts`) only produces real autonomous action when **three things agree**:

1. **§9 goal label** — `decision.chosen` must be in the spec's closed-set (§9 decisions-in-scope / §11 / §13 row labels). Checked by `LocalAgentGoalLoopRunner`.
2. **planned event** — `decision.plannedEvents[].type` must be ⊆ the agent's **§11 "Events emitted"** list (`spec.eventsEmitted`). The runner's permission-gate pre-check defers with `"planned event type(s) outside allow-list: <Type>"` otherwise.
3. **actual handler emission** — the wired handler must actually emit that planned event. If it emits a different event, the staleness check the deriver waits on never satisfies → the loop re-picks the same goal forever (silent jam).

**Bea's loop hit BOTH failure modes (2026-05-30/31, PRs #921 + #922):**
- It gated cadence on `SubLedgerReconciled`/`CloseCycleCompleted` — events its handler (`bea:accounting-readiness`) never emits → jammed on candidate-1 "Sign sub-ledger reconciliation" ~daily for 6 days, never doing real work.
- Re-pointing the planned event at `AccountingReadinessSnapshot` (what the handler actually emits) then **deferred** because that event wasn't in §11 → had to add it to §11.

**Also: derivers must be brief-aware.** Mirror Atlas's `openBriefsAddressedToAtlas()` candidate-0 — scan `AgentBriefIssued` where `issuedTo.name` matches, exclude briefIds already on any `AgentRunStarted`/`AgentRunCompleted`, count those >30min old. Bea's deriver lacked this, so her real backlog (open briefs) was structurally invisible.

**Brief-bound dispatch (triage-and-route, PR #924).** When a deriver's candidate-0 picks up an open brief, bind a run to it so it stops being re-picked: emit `AgentRunStarted{briefId, substrate:"agent-runtime"}` then `AgentRunCompleted{briefId, outcome}` (a brief is "handled" once any run event carries its briefId). The rule engine must NEVER fake delivery — close `delivered` only for briefs a deterministic handler genuinely satisfies; everything else closes `blocked` with `substrateGapsSurfaced` + a `followOnRoutes` hand-off to the executor. Classify via `expectedOutputs[].kind` (`code-pr` ⇒ route, can't self-execute).

**Permission-gate actor gotcha (cost me a CI cycle).** Run-lifecycle events (`AgentRunStarted/Completed`) must be emitted under an actor that has a **published permission policy** — use the bare parent `agent:bea` (the dispatch CLI's actor), NOT an invented sub-actor like `agent:bea:goal-loop`. `decideAppend` resolves the FULL `actor.id`: an actor with no policy + a LEGACY_PRE_A1 event type records a **legacy bypass**, and `recon:permission-gate-default` (F-031) drives bypasses to a baseline → new bypasses fail CI. A policied actor takes the Option-C allow-by-default path (no bypass). Also: any NEW `new EventStore(":memory:")` in a test file must be added to F-031's `CONSTRUCTION_CARVE_OUT_FILES` (alongside the other `*-goal-loop.test.ts`). Test fires pollute `$HOME` event.db with bypass events; clean via kill-server → `DELETE FROM events WHERE actor_id=...` → `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.

**Scheduler note:** goal-loops fire from the **main worktree** `/Users/marc/code/Bank` via launchd `com.scrooge.scheduler-tick` on the cron in `runtime/agents/metadata/<agent>.ts` (Bea: `0 6 * * *`). After merging a goal-loop fix, `git -C /Users/marc/code/Bank merge --ff-only origin/main` or the next tick runs stale code. Fire manually with `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db bun run runtime/run.ts --agent <Name> --trigger goal-loop`. Related: [[feedback_running_server_stale_branch]], [[feedback_event_store_wrong_path]].

title: Bank operating posture is indirect participant in critical market infrastructures via sponsor/correspondent banks
body:
---
name: Bank's operating posture — indirect participant in critical market infrastructures
description: Set 2026-05-07 across two decisions (D-FX-CLS-MEMBERSHIP correspondent routing; D-SAMOS-NON-CLEARING). The bank does not pursue direct membership in critical market infrastructures; access is via sponsor / correspondent banks
type: project
originSessionId: b783b4f5-e720-4ec3-a5c1-16f56fff1055
---
**Set by Marc on 2026-05-07** through two near-simultaneous decisions:

1. **D-FX-CLS-MEMBERSHIP (corrected)** — FX settles via correspondent routing through a CLS-member correspondent bank. The bank does not become a CLS Settlement Member or Third-Party-Customer.
2. **D-SAMOS-NON-CLEARING** — ZAR settlement flows via a SAMOS-sponsor bank. The bank does not become a direct SAMOS settlement participant.

**The pattern.** Capital-light, operationally lean, sponsor-routed access to critical market infrastructures. Direct memberships are operationally heavy and capital-intensive at the bank's scale; sponsor / correspondent routing preserves end-state operational outcomes while concentrating third-party-risk on a small number of well-rated sponsor banks rather than scattering it across many direct relationships.

**Likely extends to** (not yet decided, but the prior is now "indirect via sponsor unless the franchise demonstrates a specific case for direct membership"):
- **Strate** (CSDP for SA listed equities and bonds) — likely indirect CSDP-participant
- **JSE Clear** (CCP for listed derivatives) — likely indirect clearing-member
- **BankservAfrica** (low-value retail clearing) — likely not relevant for institutional bank, but if ever needed, sponsored
- **LCH SwapClear** (international OTC IRS clearing, if pursued) — likely indirect
- **SWIFT** — direct membership at BIC-level is normal regardless; the messaging path for settlement instructions

**Why this matters now.**

1. **Licence-type implications.** Most SARB Section 16 banking licences require direct SAMOS participation. The SAMOS decision implies the bank may need a different licence type — possibly a restricted / specialised banking licence, or even a non-bank investment-services arrangement under FSCA + FAIS rather than SARB. Mira + Imani + Saskia owe a near-term licence-type-confirmation deliverable. A future decision card on `D-LICENCE-TYPE` is likely.

2. **Third-party-risk concentration.** Sponsor banks become critical operational dependencies at the same level as cloud providers or core-banking vendors. Devon's third-party-risk governance is the binding control. Outsourcing & Third-Party Risk Policy + SARB Directive 3 of 2018 apply in earnest. Sponsor selection, primary + backup design, switch-testing, exit strategy.

3. **Operational resilience IBS framing.** Sponsor-failure scenarios are tier-1 BCP scenarios. IBS impact-tolerances (Devon + Helena) treat sponsor outage as critical.

4. **Capital efficiency.** Counterparty exposure to a single highly-rated sponsor (with intraday-only durations) attracts a much smaller capital charge than the equivalent bilateral / direct-membership exposure. Rohan + Camille can quantify the saving.

5. **Capital-light expansion.** New product families that touch other infrastructures (international rates clearing; cross-border equities) follow the same posture without requiring direct membership decisions to be re-litigated.

**How to apply (when authoring or recommending future decisions):**
- The default recommendation for any new market-infrastructure decision is **indirect via sponsor**, unless there's a substantive reason otherwise (cost-effective scale, regulatory requirement, franchise economics).
- The §12 trichotomy in the FX product-family deliverable (Settlement Member / Third-Party-Customer / bilateral) was a categorical error — it omitted correspondent-routing, which was the actual answer. Future market-infrastructure recommendations should always include the indirect / sponsor-routed option as a first-class alternative.
- AD status (regulatory authorisation) is independent from settlement path (operational). The bank can be a full Authorised Dealer for FX yet use a correspondent for FX settlement; it can hold deposit-taking authority yet not be a SAMOS clearing bank. Conflating these is the same categorical error.
- Concentration is the binding consideration. Multiple infrastructures via the same single sponsor is concentration risk; Devon should design the sponsor portfolio with primary + backup discipline and ideally function-split across sponsors where the operational complexity supports it.

**Open items raised by this pattern:**
- **D-LICENCE-TYPE** (urgent) — Mira + Imani + Saskia confirm the licence type consistent with indirect SAMOS participation + full AD + institutional global-markets product mix.
- Future infrastructure decisions (Strate, JSE Clear, BankservAfrica) — each should be its own decision card but the prior is now indirect-via-sponsor.
- Consolidated third-party-risk register — Devon owns; lists every sponsor / correspondent / vendor relationship at the criticality level that requires Directive-3 notification.

title: Policies implement TWO sources: regulations (external) + bank objectives (CEO/Board-approved RAS/strategic choices) — register needs Source column distinction
body:
---
name: Policies implement regulations and bank objectives
description: Set 2026-05-07 — policies have two sources, not one. They implement (a) external regulatory obligations and (b) the bank's own objectives (RAS lines, strategic-foundation choices, internal standards, operating-model rules). Refines Principle 2's upward chain.
type: project
originSessionId: a2c35cd5-9d96-424d-be9e-237ff8671f8c
---
A policy is the *what* layer in Principle 2's upward chain (Regulation → Policy → Procedure → System Capability). Marc's clarification 2026-05-07: policies implement **two distinct sources**, not just regulation:

- **Regulatory** — external rules the bank must comply with (Banks Act, FIC Act, BCBS, IFRS, POPIA, FMA, JS1/2024, JS2/2020, SARB PA Directives, FATCA, CRS, etc.). The bank does not choose these; the law imposes them.
- **Objective** — internal commitments the bank has bound itself to through governance: RAS appetite envelopes (B1–B16), strategic-foundation choices (institutional global-markets bank; ~R300m envelope; indirect-participant posture; cloud-target Azure), self-imposed reference standards (ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST SSDF, SLSA used as design references), operating-model rules (AI-driven bank P7; rules-bind-at-commencement). These are CEO-or-Board-approved internal decisions.

**Why:** Without the distinction, the obligations register conflates externally-imposed and internally-chosen sources; legitimacy chains differ (regulator vs CEO/Board); reshape requires a `Source` column on the register.

**How to apply:**

1. **Obligations register** (`Regulations/_obligations-register.md`) needs a `Source` column with values `REGULATORY` (external rule) / `OBJECTIVE` (internal commitment). Existing RAS-cited entries (ORG-PR-04, ORG-PR-10, ORG-PR-20, ORG-PR-21, ORG-CY-11, ORG-FC-18, ORG-MK-04, plus the self-imposed CY-09/CY-10/CY-12/CY-13/CY-14 reference frameworks) flip to `OBJECTIVE`. The rest stay `REGULATORY`. Some policies will appear under multiple entries (e.g. Capital Management Policy implements both Banks Act regulatory minima and RAS B2 internal buffer) — that's correct and the register already disambiguates by separate ORG-* IDs.

2. **Policy register** (`Owner Inbox/2026-05-06_policy-register.md`) Owen's pass should mirror — each policy's `source` field lists the regulations and objectives it implements.

3. **Principle 2 upward chain wording** in CLAUDE.md should read "(Regulation OR Bank Objective) → Policy → Procedure → System Capability". Worth updating when the bind-state v1.3 reshape lands its companion changes.

4. **Bank-objectives canonical source** — currently distributed across CEO decisions, RAS document, strategic-foundation document, the project memories, CLAUDE.md operating principles. Owen's canonical-source registry should explicitly name "bank objectives" as a class, and the obligations register `Source = OBJECTIVE` entries should cite into it (just as `Source = REGULATORY` entries cite the regulator instrument).

**Owners of the reshape:** Mira (obligations register Source column), Owen (policy register + canonical-source registry + Principle 2 wording in CLAUDE.md), Helena (RAS framing); coordinated by Scrooge.

title: Principle 2 merged old P2+P6: every artefact in single citable bidirectional graph; Policy heads executable chain
body:
---
name: Principle 2 — Single-graph discipline (merged P2 + old P6)
description: Current Principle 2 — merged 2026-05-11 (D-PRINCIPLES-P2-P6-MERGE). Atomic citation + single bidirectional graph; Policy heads the executable chain (sourced from Regulation OR Bank Objective); both directions equally load-bearing
type: project
originSessionId: 6e9294cc-8dc8-4604-a07d-3d8aa38c8425
---
CEO decision **D-PRINCIPLES-P2-P6-MERGE** (resolved 2026-05-11): old Principle 2 (atomic citation discipline) and old Principle 6 (single-graph discipline) merged into a single new **Principle 2 — Single-graph discipline**. Old Principle 7 (autonomous-by-default) renumbered to current Principle 6. Total principles: seven → six.

**The new Principle 2.** Every artefact in the bank sits in a single citable bidirectional graph; the citations are themselves the rule. Atomic citation and graph integrity are the same rule expressed once at the edge and once at the whole.

**The executable chain (Policy heads it):**

`Policy → Procedure → System capability → Outcome`

Policy is sourced from one or both of: **Regulation** (external obligation, in Mira's obligations register) **OR Bank Objective** (internal strategic choice, in the strategy register). A regulation without a policy is a finding; a policy that cites neither a regulation nor a bank objective is a Principle-2 violation.

**Three non-negotiable rules** — one atomic, two structural (both directions equally load-bearing):

1. **Atomic citation.** Every node carries a typed, versioned citation to the node above it. Citations are structured (urn / clause / version / as-of), held in Mira's obligations register, the policy register, and related canonical-source registers. Unsourced code or content is removed.
2. **Downward — every policy reaches a real outcome.** A policy that doesn't decompose into procedures is aspirational; a procedure without a capability is unenforced; a capability that produces no outcome is dead code. Outcomes (board packs, BA returns, STRs, FATCA / CRS XML, customer statements) are **generated**, never authored — queries over the layer below. Manual assembly at the outcome layer is a tracked Principle-3 exception.
3. **Upward — every outcome is justified by a policy.** Every event, report, screen, contract clause must trace back to a named policy and from there to its regulation or bank-objective source. No orphan capabilities. No orphan procedures. The trace is testable from any leaf.

**Operational substrate.** Anya's semantic layer, Mira's obligations register, Owen's policy register and governance framework, the procedures index, the persona/mandate library in `/Team/`, and Imani's legal-entity tree are how this principle is enforced. They are not optional. Vera (and the future CAE) consume the chain end-to-end as continuous-controls evidence.

**Why the merge:** P2 and old-P6 expressed the same rule at different scales — P2 said every artefact must carry a citation; old-P6 said those citations must form a single bidirectional graph. Old-P6's own text conceded the relationship ("Principle 2 ensures each artefact has its anchor; this principle ensures the anchors form a single, testable, bidirectional graph"). Recon harnesses and persona briefs had been inconsistent about which to cite; merging removes the ambiguity and aligns the principle count with the way the team actually reasons about the chain.

**How to apply:**
- Living documents use the new numbering (P2 = single-graph, P6 = autonomous-by-default). Historical decision records, role briefs from before 2026-05-11, and the actioned-decisions audit trail retain whatever numbering was current when written.
- When citing in new work: `Principle 2` for both atomic citation and any graph-integrity (downward or upward) rule; `Principle 6` for autonomous-by-default.
- Mira's obligations-register `Source` column must accept either a Regulation URN or a Bank-Objective URN.
- CLAUDE.md history blockquote records all three resequencings: 2026-05-06 old-P6+old-P7 → P6; 2026-05-07 new-P7 added; 2026-05-11 old-P2+old-P6 → P2, old-P7 → P6.

title: Principle 6 — bank is autonomous by default; personas are standing agent specs; humans oversee residual
body:
---
name: Principle 6 — Autonomous by default; humans oversee the residual
description: Current Principle 6 — bank is AI-run; personas are standing agents (operating specs, not characters); humans oversee the residual; default actor in every procedure step is an agent. Renumbered from old P7 on 2026-05-11
type: project
originSessionId: 6e9294cc-8dc8-4604-a07d-3d8aa38c8425
---
**Current Principle 6, renumbered from old Principle 7 on 2026-05-11** under `D-PRINCIPLES-P2-P6-MERGE`. Originally added 2026-05-07.

**Substance.**
- The bank is an autonomous AI-run institution; humans are residual overseers.
- Every persona (engineering and governance) is a standing autonomous agent. `/Team/*.md` files are operating specs (triggers, decisions in-scope, escalations, outputs, cadence, capabilities called, procedures owned), not character sheets.
- Default actor in every procedure step (per Principle 2) is an agent; human-in-the-loop is an exception with a Principle-2 citation justifying it.
- Agents run continuously (scheduled / event-triggered), not session-bound. Briefs and inboxes are agent inputs/outputs, never queues for phantom humans.
- Typed escalation channel to a named human overseer (today Marc via Scrooge); CEO's day-to-day work is reviewing escalations, not feeding tasks.
- Substrate (scheduler, event-trigger bus, agent identity, escalation channel, oversight UI) is foundational alongside event store / obligations register / IaC.
- Steady-state vs current substrate: until runtime is fully autonomous, agents are realised by Scrooge-coordinated in-session runs against their specs; each run names the substrate gap; gaps are roadmap items, not hidden.
- Vera audits this: agents without specs, missing/human-default actors without P2 citation, bypassed escalation channels, out-of-scope decisions are reportable findings.
- Reconciles with Principle 3: P3 says no step happens outside the system; P6 says every step has a named, accountable, autonomous owner inside the system.

**Why:** Marc set this on 2026-05-07 to make the autonomy intent explicit doctrine, after noticing that the prior "Scrooge voices personas in-session" model was creating an illusion of an AI bank while keeping humans as the implicit actor for everything.

**How to apply:**
- When touching any persona file, upgrade it toward agent-spec format. New personas are written as agent specs from the start.
- When writing or reviewing a procedure, check that each step's actor is a named agent; flag any human-default step that lacks a P2 citation.
- Track the substrate-gap inventory: every Scrooge-coordinated run that simulates an agent surfaces what's missing for true autonomy.
- Do not silently revert to "voicing" mode without naming the substrate gap that prevented a real agent run.

title: Product lifecycle — NPA gates go-live, not engineering; substrate build under M-phase authority precedes NPA
body:
---
name: Product lifecycle — NPA gates go-live, not engineering
description: Set 2026-05-09. The New Product Approval Policy (D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL-POLICY) is a pre-go-live gate, not a pre-build gate. Substrate construction proceeds under M-phase / D-MARKETS-SCHEMA-FOUNDATION engineering authority; NPA fires when products approach operational use.
type: project
originSessionId: 25eddba6-1506-4fa3-895c-7f1e8c9ed008
---
The bank's product lifecycle has three sequential authorities, not one:

```
[Engineering phase — D-MARKETS-SCHEMA-FOUNDATION authority; M-phase build budget]
  Ideation → Conceptualisation → Substrate design → Substrate build → Substrate verification

[NPA phase — D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL-POLICY authority; pre-go-live gate]
  Due-diligence (14 dimensions: market / credit / liquidity / op / op-readiness /
  accounting / capital / conduct / AML / model-risk / legal / infosec / privacy / tax)
  → BRC review → ProductApproved (with conditions) | ProductWithheld

[Live phase — gated by both NPA-approved AND commencement-of-trading reached]
  Controlled launch (90-day window with reduced limits)
  → Steady-state operation
  → Annual BRC review
  → Retirement
```

**NPA is the gate between engineering completion and operational use, not a gate before engineering can begin.**

## Why this matters

- M1 listed-equity substrate was ~80% built end-of-day 2026-05-08 and **that's the right state.** Under D-MARKETS-SCHEMA-FOUNDATION engineering authority. NPA hasn't run; M1 isn't go-live; bank is still pre-licence; correct.
- M2 (bonds + repo), M3 (OTC IRS), M4 (FX) substrate can be built under M-phase authority without NPA. NPA fires when each approaches commencement-of-trading.
- The bank's *first real NPA cycles run near licence-day*, when products are about to face real customers / real positions.

Aligns with `project_rules_bind_at_commencement.md`: NPA itself is CORPORATE-BIND (the bank commits to the policy at corporate existence) but its **operational gate** activates at COMMENCEMENT-BIND.

## Common confusion to avoid

Reading "every product needs NPA approval" without this distinction would imply substrate construction itself needs NPA — which would create a chicken-and-egg with M-phase build. Wrong. Substrate is engineering; NPA gates the transition to operational use.

## Authority chain

```
Regulation                 → Policy (NPA)             → Procedure (NPDD)             → System Capability
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BCBS new-product principles → D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL  → new-product-due-diligence.md → product-attestation runtime
FSCA Conduct Standards 1-3   → D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL  → product-controlled-launch.md → controlled-launch handler
Banks Act + Reg 39           → D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL  → product-pir.md               → post-implementation review
```

## How to apply

When designing a new product slice or attesting an existing one:
- Substrate-build slices cite D-MARKETS-SCHEMA-FOUNDATION (or successor M-phase authority); they do NOT require NPA pre-approval
- Pre-go-live attestations cite D-NEW-PRODUCT-APPROVAL-POLICY and produce 14 `ProductDimensionAttested` events (per the construction substrate's typed-event surface)
- The transition `ProductApproved` event fires after all 14 land green; controlled launch follows

title: Banking-specific rules bind from commencement of trading, not licence-grant; build-phase is preparation; status taxonomy: CORPORATE-BIND, LICENCE-BIND, COMMENCEMENT-BIND, CONDITIONAL-BIND
body:
---
name: Banking rules bind at commencement of trading
description: Set 2026-05-07 — banking-specific regulatory rules apply only from the date of commencement of trading as a bank; build-phase activity is preparation for compliance, not compliance itself. Pairs with project_ai_driven_bank.
type: project
originSessionId: a2c35cd5-9d96-424d-be9e-237ff8671f8c
---
Banking-specific rules (Banks Act, BCBS prudential standards operationalised via PA, FIC Act bank-MLRO provisions, FAIS Cat II/IIA, JSE rules requiring membership, ODP Conduct Standards, JS1/2024 to financial institutions, JS2/2020 margin, etc.) apply to the bank **from the date of commencement of trading as a bank**. All build-phase activity until that date is **preparation for compliance**, not compliance.

**Why:** Marc's clarification on the operating-model rule, set 2026-05-07. Pairs with the AI-driven-bank operating-model memory (`project_ai_driven_bank`): just as there's no real capital / customers / employees until licence-day, there are no in-force banking-specific obligations until commencement-of-trading. Avoids overclaiming compliance and right-sizes attention.

**How to apply:**

1. **Status taxonomy** in the obligations register (`Regulations/_obligations-register.md`) and the policy register (`Owner Inbox/2026-05-06_policy-register.md`) needs to distinguish four binding states, not one:
   - **CORPORATE-BIND** — binds today by virtue of the bank being a registered entity (Companies Act, POPIA on agent personal data, ECTA, PRECCA, tax-administration baseline, etc.). Real now.
   - **LICENCE-BIND** — binds from SARB licence-grant (most of Banks Act, the bank-specific slice of FIC Act, BCBS Pillar 1/2 via Banks Act, SARB PA Directive 3/2018, JS1/2024 for financial institutions). Pre-licence preparation today.
   - **COMMENCEMENT-BIND** — binds from active trading (FMA market-abuse, JSE rules, STT, ODP Conduct Standards 1–3 / Joint Standard 2/2020 margin, FSCA conduct standards on market activities). Pre-commencement preparation today.
   - **CONDITIONAL-BIND** — binds only when a specific state occurs (FAIS when FSP licence sought; JSE Listings Requirements when listing).

2. **Existing "IN FORCE" entries** in the registers are mis-labelled for the build phase. They mean "policy drafted / approved and ready to apply when the obligation activates" — which is **READY-FOR** status, not actual in-force. Reshape needed.

3. **RAS framing** — build-phase RAS is *preparation appetite* (what the bank tolerates while building readiness); licence-day RAS is real appetite (what the bank tolerates while operating). Helena's recalibration v2 should reflect.

4. **Audit posture** — Vera tests *readiness for compliance* in build phase (does the substrate exist; would the procedure run cleanly when triggered; would the citation chain hold), not *compliance* (no operations to enforce against). Different test bench from licence-day onward. Recon pipelines reframed accordingly.

5. **External-facing language** — regulator submissions, investor decks, public claims must say "preparing to comply" / "ready to comply on commencement" / "in build phase against [obligation]", never "complying with [banking-specific rule]" before licence-day.

6. **Dashboard metrics** — "obligations IN FORCE: 152" is misleading. Right shape: split corporate-bind / licence-bind / commencement-bind / conditional-bind, with clear status per bucket.

7. **Some obligations DO bind today** — corporate-bind set is real. Don't accidentally drop them in the reshape. Examples: Companies Act director duties, POPIA on personal-data processing of Marc + agents (where applicable), ECTA on electronic execution of contracts, PRECCA on bribery and corruption, basic tax-admin retention.

**Owners of the reshape:** Mira (obligations register status taxonomy), Owen (policy register + governance-framework reserved-matters language), Helena (RAS framing build-phase vs operating), Vera (audit posture); coordinated by Scrooge.

title: Two IRS families converged: accounting IrdSwap* (live) vs markets-CDM Irs* (dormant); historical GL backfill applied
body:
---
name: project_two_irs_event_families
description: "Two parallel IRS revaluation event families exist — accounting IrdSwap* (dormant, no live emitter) vs markets-CDM Irs* (live); granularity added to the wrong one is invisible"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b05708e8-02dc-4356-b534-06b131561073
---

The bank has **two parallel IRS event families** that are easy to confuse:

1. **`IrdSwap*` accounting/SLA family** (`platform/event-store/event-types/ird-accounting.ts`) — `IrdSwapTradeExecuted`, `IrdSwapPositionRevalued`, `IrdSwapCouponSettled`, `IrdSwapTerminated`. Consumed by the SLA posting engine (PR-IRS-002 `ird-swap-revaluation`). **`makeIrdSwapPositionRevalued` is defined but NEVER called in production** — only test fixtures. This family is **dormant** for revaluation.

2. **`Irs*` markets-CDM family** (`platform/markets/cdm/ird.ts`, registry `platform/event-store/registry/markets.ts`) — `IrsTradeBooked`, `IrsPositionRevalued` (scalar `dv01`, no tenor buckets, no bookDesignation), `IrsCouponSettlementConfirmed`. **This is what the LIVE EOD engine `runEodIrsRevaluation` (`platform/markets/eod/irs-revaluation.ts`, run by `rohan-daily-mtm`) actually emits** via `makeIrsPositionRevalued`. Also what `cva-engine.ts` reads.

**RESOLVED 2026-06-09 (D-IRS-FAMILY-CONVERGE-ACCOUNTING, PR #1121 merged):** converged onto the accounting `IrdSwap*` family. `runEodIrsRevaluation` now emits `IrdSwapPositionRevalued` (with `dv01ByTenorBucket` via shared `computeIrsDv01ByTenorBucket`/`daysToBaselMaturityBand`); booking dual-emits `IrsTradeBooked` (trade-domain, read by reval/coupon/CVA-notional/lifecycle) + `IrdSwapTradeExecuted` (accounting GL trigger); coupon→`IrdSwapCouponSettled`; `IrsPositionRevalued` emission fully retired (no production caller). CVA + SA-CCR repointed to `IrdSwapPositionRevalued`. Live IRS book now posts to GL; BA 320 IRS ladder populates. **Historical backfill** (D-IRS-HISTORICAL-GL-BACKFILL, PR #1122): idempotent `scripts/backfill-irs-historical-gl.ts` emitted IrdSwap* for the 6 pre-cutover Irs* events; RAN against home store 2026-06-09 → booked 1, revals 5; live posting subscriber auto-posted 5 balanced `ird-swap-revaluation` entries (IRS001 NPV ~R983k recognised, ACC-3300-001/002/003). Booking at-market→no day-1 posting.

**Earlier consequence (now historical):** Phase 1 (WS-BA-RETURNS-P1-SOURCING) had added `dv01ByTenorBucket`+`bookDesignation` to the dormant family; Phase 3 #1119 surfaced live swaps as substrate-gap rather than fabricating — that gap is what the convergence above closed.

**Lesson:** before adding a field to a `*PositionRevalued` event for a live metric, grep that the factory is actually *called* in production (`make<Event>` call sites minus tests), not just defined. A defined-but-uncalled factory means the field is dead on arrival. See [[feedback_merged_is_not_canonical]].

title: Live dashboard always-on — served from dedicated launchd worktree pinned to origin/main, auto-pulls every 30s
body:
---
name: reference_dashboard_supervision
description: How the live dashboard is run — supervised launchd agents + origin/main-pinned worktree (installed 2026-06-22)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 489d86b1-dcb5-420e-a15b-0201ba86693e
---

The Scrooge dashboard (http://localhost:3010) is **always-on and auto-updating** as of 2026-06-22. Setup:

- **Serves from a dedicated worktree** `/Users/marc/code/Bank/.dashboard-live` pinned to `origin/main` (NOT the main worktree). Created via `git worktree add --detach .dashboard-live origin/main`.
- **`com.scrooge.dashboard`** (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/`) — KeepAlive=true, RunAtLoad=true; runs `bun run dashboard/server.ts` from `.dashboard-live/prototype` with `BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db`, port 3010. launchd respawns it on crash/reboot (verified: kill → auto-respawn, world-sim stayed 200).
- **`com.scrooge.dashboard-autopull`** — StartInterval=30s; runs `$HOME/.local/bin/scrooge-dashboard-autopull.sh`: `git fetch origin main`; if advanced, `git reset --hard origin/main` + `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.scrooge.dashboard`. So **any code merged to main from any worktree appears within ~30s + a restart** (bun is NOT watch-mode; restart is how new code loads). Log: `~/Library/Logs/scrooge/dashboard-autopull.log` (only logs when main advances).

**ROOT CAUSE this fixed:** the launchd `event-store-archive`/scheduler jobs run from `/Users/marc/code/Bank/prototype` and commit archive markdown to a LOCAL-ONLY detached HEAD that never syncs to origin/main — so that working tree forks and goes stale, and a dashboard served from there shows old code (this is why world-sim PR #1492 wasn't visible). The dedicated worktree sidesteps the scheduler churn entirely. Don't serve the dashboard from the main worktree.

**Manage:** `launchctl bootout/bootstrap gui/$(id -u) <plist>` to reload; `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.scrooge.dashboard` to force-restart; `launchctl list | grep scrooge.dashboard` to check. **Uninstall:** bootout both + `rm` the two plists + `git worktree remove --force .dashboard-live`. Manual one-off restart still available via `scripts/restart-dashboard.sh` (#1495). NOT yet codified in repo — offer outstanding to commit the plists into `scripts/launchd/` + an install.sh for reproducibility. `recon:server-version-vs-head` gate exists to catch staleness. [[reference... ]]

A saved, reusable, modifiable reset script lives at **`/Users/marc/code/Bank/ops/reset-event-store.ts`** (deliberately OUTSIDE `prototype/` — the `recon:event-store-no-delete-callsite` gate statically fails CI on any `DELETE FROM events` under `prototype/`).

**Purpose:** build-phase clean slate. Wipes all trade lifecycle, GL postings, order flow, treasury cash positions, accounting scaffolding, trade-derived risk/liquidity/capital calcs, per-trade conduct, trade-bound messaging (`InboundMessageReceived` all carry `tradeId`) + calcs (`CalculationPerformed`), and the counterparty/client relationship layer (KYC/credit/client). **Keeps** Decisions, agent/RMS history, audit, governance, model-risk, product, obligations, policy, market reference data (`OfficialMarkAdopted`/curves), the institutional party register (all 38 `PartyRegistered` are bank-entity/agent/CEO — no counterparties exist), and platform infra.

**Cascade rule:** infra types that *describe another event by type* (`ProvenanceReclassified`→`targetEventType`, `BusDispatched`→`eventType`, `LegacyFanoutShadowed`→`triggeringEventTypes`) are deleted iff the referenced type is wiped.

**Usage:** `bun ops/reset-event-store.ts` (dry-run/preview, default), `--backup`, `--emit` (backs up first, refuses if any `production`-provenance event is in scope — verified none are), `--vacuum`, `--db <path>`. Config block at top is editable (`DELETE_PREFIXES`/`DELETE_EXACT`/`KEEP_OVERRIDE`/`CASCADE_TYPES`).

**Validated 2026-06-01** (dry-run + `--emit` on a throwaway copy): 134,491 → 54,854 events (deleted 79,637); records authorising `Decision` `D-BUILD-PHASE-EVENT-RESET`; clears `snapshots`/`bus_dispatch_claims`/`archive_partitions`; WAL-checkpoint. **Not yet run against the real store** — Marc runs it on demand. After `--emit`: restart dashboard (`cd prototype && bun run dashboard`) so projections re-derive. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-would-like-to-lazy-russell.md`. See [[feedback_sqlite_wal_delete_pattern]], [[feedback_event_store_wrong_path]].

---

description: Agent narrative provider is config-selectable (default Gemini); scheduler self-deploys via git pull --rebase on the main worktree (wedges on churn)

**Narrative provider (PR #1508, D-NARRATIVE-PROVIDER-CONFIG, 2026-06-22).** Per-agent narrative generation is provider-selectable via **`BANK_NARRATIVE_PROVIDER`** (default `gemini`; accepts `anthropic`/`claude`). Facade `runtime/narrative.ts` (`narrativeAvailable`, `tryGenerateNarrative`, `narrativeSkippedNote`) dispatches to `runtime/gemini.ts` or `runtime/claude.ts`; ~25 agents import the facade, none names a provider (Charter cmd 4). Unknown value → fail-closed `UnknownNarrativeProviderError`. Switching back to Anthropic is a config flip, never code. Distill path is separate (`BANK_DISTILL_PROVIDER`, also gemini).

**Keys live in `prototype/.env.local`; Bun AUTO-LOADS it** (CWD=main/prototype) — so the runtime reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` directly. The launchd plist `EnvironmentVariables` whitelist is `BANK_*`-only (`env-extract.ts`) and does NOT forward the provider keys — but that's moot because Bun loads `.env.local`. The `launchctl setenv` globals are NOT the source (were empty/stale — red herring). To test a key: `curl .../models?key=$KEY` (Gemini) — 403=bad/API-not-enabled, 200=ok; Anthropic `curl api.anthropic.com/v1/models -H "x-api-key:"` 401=bad.

**★Scheduler self-deploy mechanism + STALE-CODE TRAP.** The autonomous fleet runs from the **main worktree** `/Users/marc/code/Bank` (launchd `com.scrooge.scheduler-tick`, WorkingDirectory=main/prototype, `bun run scripts/scheduler-tick.ts`). scheduler-tick.ts self-updates code via in-process `git fetch origin main` + `git pull --rebase` (lines ~223/239). The archive/scheduler jobs ALSO commit derived `archive/owner-inbox/*.md` renders to main each tick (events-first VIOLATION — markdown is a render, events are canonical). Those churn commits accumulate (38 seen 2026-06-22) and CONFLICT on rebase → rebase wedges (`.git/rebase-merge/` half-done) → **the fleet runs STALE CODE indefinitely** (none of #1501/#1503/#1508 reached it until manual fix). Same anti-pattern that forced the dashboard onto `.dashboard-live`.

**Manual unblock (verified safe 2026-06-22):** `git -C /Users/marc/code/Bank rebase --abort && git -C ... reset --hard origin/main` — discards churn (re-derivable; archive DATA lives in `~/.local/share/bank/archives/` outside repo; verify no hand-authored commits first via `git cherry origin/main ORIG_HEAD`, `-`=already-upstream). Do NOT `git clean` (would nuke `.dashboard-live/`, `graphify-out/`). reset/abort don't trip the [[reference_main_worktree_write_guard]] (no commit/rebase/push); scheduler-tick's own rebase IS allowlisted via `BANK_ALLOW_MAIN_WORKTREE_WRITE=1`.

**DURABLE FIX — ✅BUILT+DEPLOYED (PR #1509, D-SCHEDULER-DEPLOY-DECOUPLE, 2026-06-22).** Scheduler now runs from a dedicated clean worktree **`/Users/marc/code/Bank/.scheduler-live`** (detached, pinned origin/main), kept current by launchd **`com.scrooge.scheduler-autopull`** (fetch -q + `reset --hard origin/main`, exit 0). scheduler-tick.ts self-update REMOVED (no execSync at all; only explanatory comments mention git). The render-commit block WAS the self-update (fetch/rebase were side-effects of pushing renders) → removing it did both parts. **Nothing commits to main now** → `env-extract` no longer injects `BANK_ALLOW_MAIN_WORKTREE_WRITE=1` (guard allowlist empty; only Marc's TTY writes main). All 4 jobs (scheduler-tick, scheduler-autopull, event-store-archive, golden-source-integrity-tick) rooted at `.scheduler-live`. **DEPLOY (done; re-runnable):** worktree add --detach .scheduler-live origin/main → cp main's `.env.local` into it (gitignored!) → bun install → bootout ALL scrooge jobs (clears domain; bootstrap hits `Input/output error 5` if a label lingers) → run `.scheduler-live/.../install.sh` (derives SCHEDULER_LIVE_DIR from git-common-dir) → kickstart autopull. ★GEMINI QUOTA: narratives route to Gemini correctly but hit **429 "exceeded your current quota / check billing"** (also seen 503 high-demand) on gemini-2.5-flash-lite — free-tier/quota limit, retryable, degrades gracefully (runs still ok). Needs Marc to enable billing/raise quota for reliable narratives. [[reference_dashboard_supervision]] [[reference_main_worktree_write_guard]]
